rows.verbatim:
Upon completion of the work, promptly remove plant, including ranges,
buoys, piles, and other markers or obstructions.
rows.normalized: Contractor must promptly remove plant (ranges, buoys, piles, markers/obstructions) upon completion of work.

rows.verbatim:
Final estimates will be subject to deductions or correction of deductions
previously made because of excessive overdepth, dredging outside of
authorized areas, or disposal of material in an unauthorized manner.
rows.normalized: Final estimates will be subject to deductions for contractor's excessive overdepth, unauthorized-area dredging, or unauthorized disposal.

rows.verbatim:
No shoals or lumps above contract depth, as evidenced by multi-beam
sounding will be accepted.
rows.normalized: No shoals or lumps above contract depth, as evidenced by multi-beam sounding, will be accepted.

rows.verbatim:
The work under this contract requires use of the US Army Corps of Engineers (USACE)
Dredging Quality Management (DQM) Program to monitor all dredge plants at all times
throughout the contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor must use the USACE DQM Program to monitor all dredge plants at all times throughout the contract.

rows.verbatim:
DQM monitoring is required on all equipment (to be called plants) used on this contract
to excavate, transport, or place dredged material.
rows.normalized: DQM monitoring is required on all equipment used to excavate, transport, or place dredged material.

rows.verbatim: At least one week prior to the target date, the DQM Center must be contacted to verbally coordinate a specific date and location.
rows.normalized: Contractor must contact the DQM Center at least one week prior to the target date to verbally coordinate a specific date and location.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor must then follow up this conversation with a written email
confirmation.
rows.normalized: Contractor must follow up the verbal coordination with a written email confirmation.

rows.verbatim: Any changes must be reported in the
rows.normalized: Contractor must report any changes (sentence truncated by page break; further detail not captured).

rows.verbatim:
Current certification from the DQM Center for all dredge plants to be used under this
contract is required.
rows.normalized: Contractor must have current DQM Center certification for all dredge plants used under this contract.

rows.verbatim:
DQM certification is contingent upon the Contractor’s system’s ability to meet the
performance requirements as outlined in SYSTEM TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS and
OPERATIONAL PERFORMANCE, REPORTING AND QA, including all
subparagraphs.
rows.normalized: If the Contractor's system fails to meet the performance requirements in SYSTEM TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS and OPERATIONAL PERFORMANCE, REPORTING AND QA, DQM certification is contingent on meeting them.

rows.verbatim:
If performance requirements are not met and maintained, DQM
certification may be revoked.
rows.normalized: If performance requirements are not met and maintained, DQM certification may be revoked.

rows.verbatim:
Contact the DQM Center at dqm-support@usace.army.mil at least three weeks prior to
certification expiration, to schedule and coordinate QA checks for certification renewal.
rows.normalized: Contractor must contact the DQM Center at least three weeks prior to certification expiration to schedule QA checks for renewal.

rows.verbatim:
Recertification is required for changes in sensor type or location as well as any yard work
that produces modification to reported values.
rows.normalized: Recertification is required for sensor type/location changes or yard work that modifies reported values.

rows.verbatim:
Any changes must be reported in theW912P726RA022
Page 279 of 645SOLICITATION
sensor log section of the DPIP.
rows.normalized: The Contractor must report any changes in the sensor log section of the DPIP.

rows.verbatim: the sensors or hardware must not be disconnected or removed from the plant
rows.normalized: Contractor must not disconnect or remove DQM sensors/hardware from the plant to retain DQM certification.

rows.verbatim: If the system is powered down, calibration coefficients must be retained.
rows.normalized: If the system is powered down, the Contractor must retain calibration coefficients.

rows.verbatim: Contractor/subcontractor personnel who are familiar with the instrumentation and can recalibrate the sensors must be on site during the QA process.
rows.normalized: Contractor/subcontractor personnel familiar with the instrumentation must be on site during the QA process.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor will coordinate pickup times and locations and provide transportation to and from any vessel with a DQM system to team personnel in a timely manner.
rows.normalized: Contractor will coordinate pickup times/locations and provide transportation to/from any DQM-equipped vessel for team personnel in a timely manner.

rows.verbatim: If additional safety equipment is needed, such as eye protection, safety harnesses, work gloves, or personal location beacons— the Contractor must provide these items to the DQM QA team while on site.
rows.normalized: If additional safety equipment is needed, Contractor must provide it to the DQM QA team while on site.

rows.verbatim: It is the Contractor's obligation to inform the DQM QA team if the location designated for the QA checks has any site-specific safety concerns prior to their arrival on site.
rows.normalized: Contractor is obligated to inform the DQM QA team of site-specific safety concerns at the QA check location before their arrival.

rows.verbatim: A digital copy of the DPIP must be on file with the DQM Center.
rows.normalized: Contractor must have a digital copy of the DPIP on file with the DQM Center.

rows.verbatim: While working on site, the Contractor will maintain on the plant a copy of the DPIP, which is always easily accessible to Government personnel.
rows.normalized: Contractor will maintain an accessible copy of the DPIP on the plant while working on site.

rows.verbatim: This document must accurately describe the sensors used, the configuration of the system, how sensor data will be collected, how quality control on the data will be performed, and how the sensors/data-reporting equipment will be calibrated and repaired if it fails.
rows.normalized: The DPIP must accurately describe sensors, configuration, data collection, quality control, and calibration/repair procedures.

rows.verbatim: A description of the computed plant-specific data and how the sensor data will be transmitted to the DQM database must also be included.
rows.normalized: The DPIP must also include a description of computed plant-specific data and how sensor data will be transmitted to the DQM database.

rows.verbatim: Prior to the start of work any addendum or modifications made to the plan after its original submission must be submitted to the DQM Center.
rows.normalized: Contractor must submit any DPIP addenda/modifications to the DQM Center prior to the start of work.

rows.verbatim: Any changes to the computation methods must be approved by the DQM Center prior to their implementation.
rows.normalized: Contractor must obtain DQM Center approval for any computation method changes before implementation.

rows.verbatim: The log must contain a three-year history of sensor maintenance, including the time of the sensor failures (and subsequent repairs, replacements, installations, modifications, and calibrations), the time and results of sensor calibrations, the time of sensor replacements, and the time that backup sensor systems were initiated to provide the required data.
rows.normalized: Contractor's sensor log must contain a three-year history of sensor maintenance events and related timing/results.

rows.verbatim: It must also contain the name of the person responsible for the sensor work.
rows.normalized: The sensor log must also contain the name of the person responsible for the sensor work.

rows.verbatim: Keep a log of sensor repairs, replacements, installations, modifications, and calibrations in the DPIP.
rows.normalized: Contractor must keep a log of sensor repairs, replacements, installations, modifications, and calibrations in the DPIP.

rows.verbatim: A plant does not have to be transmitting data between jobs; however, to retain its DQM certification, the sensors or hardware must not be disconnected or removed from the plant.
rows.normalized: To retain DQM certification, the Contractor must not disconnect or remove sensors/hardware from the plant between jobs.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor must provide, operate, and maintain all hardware and software to meet these specifications for the respective plant types on the contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide, operate, and maintain all hardware and software to meet the specifications for the applicable plant types.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor is responsible for the repairs, replacements, installations, modifications, and calibrations of the sensors and any other equipment needed to collect and transmit the required data.
rows.normalized: Contractor is responsible for repairs, replacements, installations, modifications, and calibrations of sensors and other equipment needed to collect and transmit required data.

rows.verbatim: Sensors installed must be capable of collecting and reporting parameters at the specified interval, accuracy, precision, and resolution as described in DATA PARAMETERS BY PLANT TYPE, including all subparagraphs.
rows.normalized: Installed sensors must be capable of collecting and reporting parameters at the specified interval, accuracy, precision, and resolution per DATA PARAMETERS BY PLANT TYPE.

rows.verbatim: Data will be logged and archived locally onboard the plant as a backup to transmitted data as described in DATA BACKUP REQUIREMENTS.
rows.normalized: Data must be logged and archived locally onboard the plant as a backup per DATA BACKUP REQUIREMENTS.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor must provide an easily accessible visual display onboard the plant that displays in real time the raw parameters collected by the system in the same units as are used for data submitted to DQM.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide an easily accessible onboard visual display showing real-time raw parameters in the same units as data submitted to DQM.

rows.verbatim: In the event a reported parameter is calculated based on multiple sensors, the sensor values as used in the equation must be visible in addition to the required parameter.
rows.normalized: If a reported parameter is calculated from multiple sensors, the individual sensor values used in the equation must also be visible.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor is responsible for acquiring, installing, and maintaining all necessary hardware and software to ensure reliable internet connectivity for data transmission to the DQM web service.
rows.normalized: Contractor is responsible for acquiring, installing, and maintaining hardware/software for reliable internet connectivity to transmit data to the DQM web service.

rows.verbatim: The internet connection must support real-time data transmission and provide sufficient bandwidth to clear any queued data when connectivity is restored after an outage.
rows.normalized: The internet connection (provided by Contractor) must support real-time data transmission and sufficient bandwidth to clear queued data after an outage.

rows.verbatim: Data collected must be transmitted to the DQM web service in real-time, in accordance with the standards outlined in DATA PARAMETERS BY PLANT TYPE and all related subparagraphs.
rows.normalized: Collected data must be transmitted to the DQM web service in real-time per DATA PARAMETERS BY PLANT TYPE standards.

rows.verbatim: Scow data transmission must be fully automated end-to-end.
rows.normalized: Scow data transmission must be fully automated end-to-end.

rows.verbatim: When a relay is used: (a) the scow must transmit to the relay no less frequently than every 4 hours, and (b) the relay must forward to the DQM web service immediately and automatically upon receipt.
rows.normalized: If a relay is used, the scow must transmit to the relay at least every 4 hours, and the relay must forward data to the DQM web service immediately and automatically upon receipt.

rows.verbatim: If internet connectivity is lost, the web service is unavailable, or data cannot be transmitted for any reason, unsent data should be queued and transmitted immediately upon restoration of connectivity.
rows.normalized: If connectivity/transmission fails, the Contractor should queue unsent data and transmit it immediately upon restoration.

rows.verbatim: Transmission should begin with the oldest data in the queue and continue until real-time transmission resumes.
rows.normalized: Queued data transmission should begin with the oldest data and continue until real-time transmission resumes.

rows.verbatim: Failure to transmit within timeframes may be treated as non-compliance and/or result in revocation of the plant’s DQM certification.
rows.normalized: Failure to transmit data within required timeframes may result in non-compliance findings or certification revocation.

rows.verbatim:
Data must be collected and transmitted at set intervals (which vary by plant type and
activity state) as outlined in the table below.
rows.normalized: Contractor must collect and transmit data at set intervals per the table, varying by plant type and activity state.

rows.verbatim:
Raw sensor samples reported in a data string
must be acquired no more than 1 second before the timestamp of that string.
rows.normalized: Contractor must acquire raw sensor samples reported in a data string no more than 1 second before the timestamp of that string.

rows.verbatim:
Averaged or computed parameters
must be derived from samples acquired within the reporting
interval as outlined in the table below.
rows.normalized: Contractor must derive averaged or computed parameters from samples acquired within the reporting interval per the table.

rows.verbatim:
Any sensor data averaging or calculations
performed externally to the sensors must be documented in the DPIP.
rows.normalized: Contractor must document in the DPIP any sensor data averaging or calculations performed externally to the sensors.

rows.verbatim:
A data point must be recorded within 1 second of a
bucket “dig” or “dump” event occurring.
rows.normalized: Contractor must record a data point within 1 second of a bucket dig or dump event for Mechanical plant type.

rows.verbatim:
A data point must be recorded within 1
second of the hull status going from closed to open and again within
1 second of the hull status going from open to closed.
rows.normalized: Contractor must record a data point within 1 second of the hull status changing from closed to open and again within 1 second of it changing from open to closed, for Scow Open Water Placement.

rows.verbatim:
This interval must
always remain consistent for the dredge plant.
rows.normalized: Contractor must keep the reporting interval consistent for the dredge plant (Scow Open Water Placement).

rows.verbatim: Collected sensor data will be compiled into correctly formatted data strings for transmission to DQM.
rows.normalized: Collected sensor data must be compiled into correctly formatted data strings for transmission to DQM.

rows.verbatim:
Hopper: XML
Scow: XML
Pipeline: JSON
Mechanical: JSON
rows.normalized: Data string format must follow plant-type-specific formats: Hopper/Scow in XML, Pipeline/Mechanical in JSON.

rows.verbatim: All data strings contain a minimum of two data parameters, a plant identifier assigned by the DQM Center and a Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) stamp based on a 24-hour format (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS).
rows.normalized: All data strings must contain at minimum a DQM-assigned plant identifier and a UTC timestamp in specified format.

rows.verbatim: If a parameter is not applicable or otherwise missing, it will be omitted from the data string.
rows.normalized: If a parameter is not applicable or missing, it must be omitted from the data string.

rows.verbatim: Between these events, report the data at an equal interval from 6 to 12 seconds.
rows.normalized: Between hull status events, the Contractor must report data at an equal interval of 6 to 12 seconds.

rows.verbatim: Data will be logged locally onboard the plant as a backup of transmitted data.
rows.normalized: Contractor's system will log data locally onboard the plant as a backup of transmitted data.

rows.verbatim: An archive of all data sent to the DQM Center in the format that it was originally collected and transmitted must be maintained.
rows.normalized: Contractor must maintain an archive of all data sent to the DQM Center in its originally collected/transmitted format.

rows.verbatim: This archive will be preserved by the Contractor for a minimum of one year past the end of the contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor must preserve the archive for a minimum of one year past the end of the contract.

rows.verbatim: At the completion of dredging activities all data gaps must be filled or addressed.
rows.normalized: Contractor must fill or address all data gaps at completion of dredging activities.

rows.verbatim: When data backup includes unresolved data gaps the Contractor must follow the guidance described in DATA GAPS.
rows.normalized: If data backup includes unresolved data gaps, Contractor must follow the DATA GAPS guidance.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor’s data transmission system must be operational at the start of dredging operations and certified prior to moving dredge material on the contract (see paragraph CERTIFICATION).
rows.normalized: Contractor's data transmission system must be operational at start of dredging operations and certified before moving dredge material.

rows.verbatim: The plant must maintain DQM certification and remain compliant throughout the duration of the contract.
rows.normalized: Plant must maintain DQM certification and remain compliant throughout the contract.

rows.verbatim: A work event message includes all required sensor data, computed parameters, and a timestamp corresponding to the event or interval.
rows.normalized: Each work event message must include all required sensor data, computed parameters, and a timestamp.

rows.verbatim: In addition to real-time work event messages, submissions of “state data” are also required for hoppers, pipeline, and mechanical plant types.
rows.normalized: Contractor is required to submit state data for hoppers, pipeline, and mechanical plant types.

rows.verbatim: State data entries are submitted daily through the DQM Contractor Management Site from the first day of dredging activity on the contract through the final day.
rows.normalized: Contractor must submit state data entries daily via the DQM Contractor Management Site from the first through final day of dredging activity.

rows.verbatim: State data must be submitted daily, reporting on all activities for the prior day.
rows.normalized: Contractor must submit state data daily, reporting on prior-day activities.

rows.verbatim: Prior to commencement of project startup and at the completion of work DQM must be notified by emailing dqm-support@usace.army.mil.
rows.normalized: Contractor must notify DQM by email prior to project startup and at completion of work.

rows.verbatim: The notification must include the plants working on the project, estimated project duration, and project personnel who need access to DQM.
rows.normalized: Contractor's notification must include plants working on the project, estimated duration, and personnel needing DQM access.

rows.verbatim: In the event of a system outage that results in a data gap which cannot be filled with backup data, provide a clear explanation documenting the cause and duration of the gap.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide a clear explanation documenting the cause and duration of any unfillable data gap.

rows.verbatim: Record this explanation using the DQM Contractor Management Site within 48 hours.
rows.normalized: Contractor must record the data-gap explanation in the DQM Contractor Management Site within 48 hours.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor will submit a response within 48 hours of receiving any QA notification identifying immediate mitigations and an estimated restoration schedule.
rows.normalized: Contractor will submit a response within 48 hours of receiving any QA notification, identifying immediate mitigations and an estimated restoration schedule.

rows.verbatim: All notifications, actions, and supporting records will be entered in DQM Contractor Management Site.
rows.normalized: Contractor will enter all notifications, actions, and supporting records into the DQM Contractor Management Site.

rows.verbatim: If hardware problems occur, or if a part of the system is physically damaged, the Contractor is responsible for repairs.
rows.normalized: If hardware problems occur or a part of the system is physically damaged, Contractor is responsible for repairs.

rows.verbatim: Sensor failures must be documented on the DQM Contractor Management Site.
rows.normalized: Contractor must document sensor failures on the DQM Contractor Management Site.

rows.verbatim: Corrective action (repair, replacement, or recalibration) must be completed within 48 hours of discovery.
rows.normalized: Contractor must complete corrective action (repair, replacement, or recalibration) within 48 hours of discovery.

rows.verbatim: If 48-hour completion is not feasible, the Contractor must notify the DQM Center before the 48-hour deadline with cause and estimated completion date.
rows.normalized: If 48-hour completion is not feasible, Contractor must notify the DQM Center before the 48-hour deadline with cause and estimated completion date.

rows.verbatim: Upon completion of repairs, replacements, installations, modifications, or calibrations, notify the DQM Center.
rows.normalized: Upon completion of repairs, replacements, installations, modifications, or calibrations, Contractor must notify the DQM Center.

rows.verbatim:
Clear and accurate draft marks
Dragarm depth chain or calibrated pressure sensor
Ullage tape
Refractometer
Water-sampling device
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide the listed QA equipment (draft marks, dragarm depth chain/pressure sensor, ullage tape, refractometer, water-sampling device) on hopper dredges.

rows.verbatim: Suction mouth depth chain/tape or calibrated pressure sensor
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide a suction mouth depth chain/tape or calibrated pressure sensor as QA equipment on pipeline dredges.

rows.verbatim: Bucket depth chain/tape or calibrated pressure sensor
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide a bucket depth chain/tape or calibrated pressure sensor as QA equipment on mechanical dredges.

rows.verbatim:
Clear and accurate draft marks
Ullage tape
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide draft marks and ullage tape as QA equipment on scows.

rows.verbatim: Transmit all data in XML message bundles (see DATA FORMAT).
rows.normalized: Contractor must transmit all hopper sensor data in XML message bundles.

rows.verbatim: If the plant is new to using DQM, please contact the DQM Center for a Plant Identifier.
rows.normalized: If the plant is new to DQM, Contractor must contact the DQM Center for a Plant Identifier.

rows.verbatim: Load number for each plant will begin at number 1 at the start of the contract and will increment by one at the completion of each placement event.
rows.normalized: Contractor's system must number each plant's loads starting at 1, incrementing by one per placement event.

rows.verbatim: Load number sequence will be unique to each plant on the contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor's load number sequence must be unique to each plant on the contract.

rows.verbatim: Whenever possible, calculate the load number using sensors aboard the plant with a mathematically repeatable routine.
rows.normalized: Contractor must calculate load number using onboard sensors with a repeatable routine whenever possible.

rows.verbatim: Make efforts to include logic that avoids false load number increments.
rows.normalized: Contractor must include logic to avoid false load number increments.

rows.verbatim: If manual increment of the load number is performed, pay extra attention to this value in the quality control process.
rows.normalized: If load number is manually incremented, Contractor must pay extra attention to this value during quality control.

rows.verbatim: Report the date and time to the nearest second and referenced to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) time based on a 24-hour format (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS).
rows.normalized: Contractor must report date/time to the nearest second in UTC 24-hour format.

rows.verbatim: The reported time must be the time reported by the Global Positioning System (GPS) in the National Marine Electronics Association (NMEA) data string.
rows.normalized: Reported time must be the GPS time from the NMEA data string.

rows.verbatim: Horizontal positions must be reported for all dragheads.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report horizontal positions for all dragheads.

rows.verbatim: The COG must be accurate to within 5 degrees and reported to the nearest whole degree with values from 000 (true north) to 359 degrees referenced to a clockwise positive direction convention.
rows.normalized: Contractor must ensure course-over-ground (COG) is accurate to within 5 degrees and reported to the nearest whole degree per specified convention.

rows.verbatim: An “open” status must be reported as the bin starts to open, and a “closed” status must be indicated only once the bin is fully closed.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report an 'open' status as the bin starts to open and a 'closed' status only once the bin is fully closed.

rows.verbatim: For bins with multiple doors or pockets, the “open”/”closed” status must correspond to the compartment which is first to open and last to close.
rows.normalized: For bins with multiple doors or pockets, contractor must ensure the open/closed status corresponds to the compartment that is first to open and last to close.

rows.verbatim: Obtain location using a positioning system operating with a minimum accuracy level of 3-10 feet horizontal Circular Error Probable (CEP).
rows.normalized: Contractor must obtain location using a positioning system with minimum accuracy of 3-10 feet horizontal CEP.

rows.verbatim: Report positions as Latitude/Longitude World Geodetic System 1984 (WGS 84) in decimal degrees with South Latitude and West Longitude values reported as negative.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report vessel positions as WGS 84 lat/long in decimal degrees with negative South/West values.

rows.verbatim: Record vessel horizontal positioning as geographic coordinates of the vessel as indicated by the location of the GPS antenna.
rows.normalized: Contractor must record vessel horizontal positioning as geographic coordinates of the GPS antenna location.

rows.verbatim: Describe any offset calculations from the GPS antenna(s) in the DPIP.
rows.normalized: Contractor must describe any GPS antenna offset calculations in the DPIP.

rows.verbatim: Report positions as Latitude/Longitude WGS 84 in decimal degrees with South Latitude and West Longitude values reported as negative.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report draghead positions as WGS 84 lat/long in decimal degrees with negative South/West values.

rows.verbatim: Record draghead horizontal positioning as geographic coordinates of the heel on the centerline of the draghead(s).
rows.normalized: Contractor must record draghead horizontal positioning as coordinates of the heel on the draghead centerline.

rows.verbatim: Provide vessel course-over-ground (COG) using industry-standard equipment.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide vessel COG using industry-standard equipment.

rows.verbatim: Provide vessel speed-over-ground in knots using industry-standard equipment with a minimum accuracy of 1 knot and resolution to the nearest 0.1 knot.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide vessel speed-over-ground in knots with minimum accuracy of 1 knot and 0.1 knot resolution.

rows.verbatim: Provide vessel heading using industry-standard equipment.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide vessel heading using industry-standard equipment.

rows.verbatim: The only permissible values are “open” and “closed”.
rows.normalized: Hull status reported values are limited to 'open' and 'closed'.

rows.verbatim:
Obtain the variation of the water level from the vertical datum for the river stage or tidal
gage using appropriate equipment to give the water level with an accuracy of ± 0.1 foot
and a resolution of 0.01 foot.
rows.normalized: Contractor must obtain vertical correction (tide) with accuracy of ± 0.1 foot and resolution of 0.01 foot.

rows.verbatim:
Enter vertical correction values above the project datum
with a positive sign and those below with a negative sign.
rows.normalized: Contractor must enter vertical correction values above datum as positive, below as negative.

rows.verbatim:
Use datum and gage described
in the dredging specification and indicate in the state events when changing gages.
rows.normalized: Contractor must use the datum/gage described in the dredging specification and indicate state events when changing gages.

rows.verbatim:
Report all draft measurements in decimal feet with an accuracy of ± 0.1 ft and a
resolution of 0.01 ft relative to observed physical draft readings in calm water.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report draft measurements in decimal feet, accuracy ± 0.1 ft, resolution 0.01 ft.

rows.verbatim: Values for the forward draft and aft draft will be reported.
rows.normalized: Contractor will report forward and aft draft values.

rows.verbatim: The reported draft values are the averages of the respective port and starboard physical draft mark readings.
rows.normalized: Reported draft values must be the averages of port and starboard physical draft mark readings.

rows.verbatim:
Report vessel displacement in long tons to the nearest tenth, based on the most accurate
method available for the plant.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report vessel displacement in long tons to the nearest tenth, using most accurate method available.

rows.verbatim:
The minimum standard of accuracy for displacement is
interpolation from the displacement table, based on the average draft.
rows.normalized: Contractor's displacement accuracy must meet at minimum interpolation from the displacement table based on average draft.

rows.verbatim:
Report empty displacement in long tons to the nearest tenth, which is the lightship value
of the plant, or the weight of the vessel with no material in the bin, adjusted for fuel and
water consumption.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report empty displacement in long tons to the nearest tenth (lightship value adjusted for fuel/water).

rows.verbatim:
Report forward and aft ullage distances in decimal feet with an accuracy of ± 0.1 ft and a
resolution of 0.01 ft relative to the ullage table reference point (typically the top of
coaming) at the forward and aft extents of the bin along the centerline.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report forward/aft ullage distances in decimal feet, accuracy ± 0.1 ft, resolution 0.01 ft.

rows.verbatim:
Mount sensors to avoid discharge flume turbulence, foam, and any structure that could
produce sidelobe errors.
rows.normalized: Contractor must mount ullage sensors to avoid discharge flume turbulence, foam, and sidelobe-error-producing structures.

rows.verbatim:
If sensors must be offset from the centerline of the bin, the
sensors should be offset to opposite sides of the vessel.
rows.normalized: If sensors must be offset from bin centerline, contractor should offset sensors to opposite sides of vessel.

rows.verbatim:
If more than one fore or one aft sensor is used, place the sensors near the corners of the bin, and report the average value
of the fore sensors and the average value of the aft sensors.
rows.normalized: If more than one fore/aft sensor is used, contractor must place sensors near bin corners and report average fore/aft values.

rows.verbatim: Depths must be reported for all dragheads.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report draghead depths for all dragheads.

rows.verbatim: Densities must be reported for each draghead and pumpout path.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report slurry densities for each draghead and pumpout path.

rows.verbatim: Dredges with multiple pumps per side must report RPM for the pump that best describes the dredging process.
rows.normalized: For dredges with multiple pumps per side, contractor must report RPM for the pump that best describes the dredging process.

rows.verbatim:
Report bin volume in cubic yards to the nearest tenth, based on the most accurate method
available for the dredge.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report bin volume in cubic yards to the nearest tenth, using most accurate method available.

rows.verbatim:
The minimum standard of accuracy for bin volume is
interpolation from the certified bin volume table, based on the average fore and aft ullage
soundings.
rows.normalized: Contractor's bin volume accuracy must meet at minimum interpolation from the certified bin volume table based on average ullage soundings.

rows.verbatim:
Report draghead depths with an accuracy of ± 0.5 foot and a resolution to the nearest 0.1
foot as measured from the surface of the water with no tidal adjustments.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report draghead depths with accuracy ± 0.5 ft, resolution 0.1 ft, measured from water surface with no tidal adjustments.

rows.verbatim:
Use a density-metering device, calibrated according to the manufacturer’s specifications,
to record the slurry density from each pump being used to move material in any phase of
the dredging process to the nearest 0.001 grams per cubic centimeter (g/cc) with an
accuracy of ± 0.01 g/cc.
rows.normalized: Contractor must use a calibrated density-metering device to record slurry density to the nearest 0.001 g/cc with accuracy ± 0.01 g/cc.

rows.verbatim:
If the manufacturer does not specify a frequency of
recalibration, conduct calibration prior to commencement of work.
rows.normalized: If the manufacturer does not specify a recalibration frequency for density metering, contractor must calibrate prior to commencement of work.

rows.verbatim:
Use a flow-metering device, calibrated according to the manufacturer’s specifications, to
record the slurry velocity from each pump being used to move material in any phase of

rows.verbatim: USACE shall coordinate with the Water Board, in conjunction with the DMMO, to determine the extent of elevated concentrations and appropriate measures during the sediment characterization and episode approval process pursuant to Provision 2 of this Order.
rows.normalized: The party performing dredging must coordinate with the Water Board and DMMO to determine the extent of elevated contaminant concentrations and appropriate measures during sediment characterization and episode approval.

rows.verbatim: All dredged sediment and any water entrained during dredging will be completely contained within the placement cell.
rows.normalized: All dredged sediment and entrained water must be completely contained within the placement cell at Cullinan.

rows.verbatim: This Order requires USACE to submit an annual Integrated Alternatives Analysis (IAA) of disposal options for dredged sediments from the Project under Provision 6 of this Order.
rows.normalized: USACE must submit an annual Integrated Alternatives Analysis (IAA) of disposal options for dredged sediments under Provision 6 of this Order.

rows.verbatim: This Order requires USACE to provide a technical report that documents monitoring efforts designed to evaluate the water quality impacts of the dredged material discharge on waters of the State, pursuant to California Water Code (Water Code) section 13383.
rows.normalized: USACE must provide a technical report documenting monitoring of water quality impacts of dredged material discharge, per Water Code section 13383.

rows.verbatim: USACE is a participant in the RMP and will contribute $508,000 annually, following the dredging season, to the program by funding the United States Geological Survey (USGS) to monitor suspended sediments at an array of locations in the Bay under Provision 9 of this Order.
rows.normalized: USACE will contribute $508,000 annually to the RMP, following the dredging season, via USGS funding under Provision 9.

rows.verbatim: To characterize dredged sediment for disposal or placement, USACE will conduct full Tier III sediment sampling and characterization and submit completed reports to the DMMO for approval every three to five years for annually dredged channels, or as determined by the DMMO for all other channels.
rows.normalized: USACE will conduct full Tier III sediment sampling/characterization and submit reports to the DMMO for approval every three to five years (or as DMMO determines).

rows.verbatim: USACE will submit to the DMMO requests for Tier I testing exemptions for dredging episodes in channels that have Tier III results from the last three to five years, or as determined by the DMMO.
rows.normalized: USACE will submit Tier I testing exemption requests to the DMMO for channels with recent Tier III results, or as DMMO determines.

rows.verbatim: Each dredging episode must be approved in writing by the Executive Officer pursuant to Provision 7 of this Order.
rows.normalized: Each dredging episode must be approved in writing by the Executive Officer under Provision 7 before proceeding.

rows.verbatim: USACE will conduct eelgrass surveys and light monitoring in accordance with Provision 4 of this Order, consistent with the June 9, 2011, Programmatic Essential Fish Habitat Consultation Agreement between the U.S. EPA, USACE, and NMFS.
rows.normalized: USACE will conduct eelgrass surveys and light monitoring in accordance with Provision 4.

rows.verbatim: This Order requires USACE to continue monitoring under Provision 11 to evaluate potential fish entrainment during hopper dredging by the USACE-owned ship, the Essayons, in the San Francisco Bay Area.
rows.normalized: USACE must continue fish entrainment monitoring during hopper dredging by the Essayons under Provision 11.

rows.verbatim: Changes to this monitoring plan must be approved in writing by the Executive Officer pursuant to Provision 11.
rows.normalized: Changes to the monitoring plan must be approved in writing by the Executive Officer under Provision 11.

rows.verbatim: An entrainment sampling apparatus will sample dredged sediment that enters through both drag arms by passing the dredged sediment slurry through a rectangular shaped sieve.
rows.normalized: The entrainment sampling apparatus will sample dredged sediment entering both drag arms via a rectangular sieve.

rows.verbatim: The biological monitors will sort, examine, and document the accumulated material.
rows.normalized: Biological monitors will sort, examine, and document the accumulated material.

rows.verbatim: Other opportunistic monitoring methods (e.g., observing water surface in the hopper, sampling during water calibration and hopper flushing events) will also be conducted when relevant opportunities arise.
rows.normalized: Other opportunistic monitoring methods will also be conducted when relevant opportunities arise.

rows.verbatim: To avoid, minimize, and compensate for the entrainment impacts described above, USACE will implement measures included in the Project as described in EA/EIR Section 2.3.1.5 and the application for this Order, as well as the mitigation required in Provision 10 of this Order.
rows.normalized: USACE will implement avoidance/minimization/compensation measures for entrainment impacts per EA/EIR Section 2.3.1.5 and Provision 10 mitigation requirements.
rows.section_ref: 17. Avoidance, Minimization, and Compensatory Mitigation Measures for Entrainment Impacts

rows.verbatim: When conducting Phase 1, this Order requires USACE to compensate for unavoidable in-Bay hopper dredging entrainment impacts by either purchasing longfin smelt mitigation credits at a resource agency-approved habitat conservation bank or placing a specified volume of dredged sediment at a non-aquatic beneficial reuse site for tidal wetland restoration as required in Provision 10, in a similar manner to USFWS longfin smelt mitigation described above.
rows.normalized: If conducting Phase 1, USACE must compensate for unavoidable in-Bay hopper dredging entrainment impacts by purchasing longfin smelt mitigation credits or placing dredged sediment for tidal wetland restoration, per Provision 10.
rows.section_ref: 17. Avoidance, Minimization, and Compensatory Mitigation Measures for Entrainment Impacts

rows.verbatim: Therefore, USACE is required to compensate for significant impacts, reducing them to less than significant in combination with the standard practices described in the EA/EIR Section 2.3.1.5 and the hopper dredging specific practices described below.
rows.normalized: USACE is required to compensate for significant impacts, reducing them to less than significant, using standard and hopper-dredging-specific practices.
rows.section_ref: 17. Avoidance, Minimization, and Compensatory Mitigation Measures for Entrainment Impacts

rows.verbatim:
No dredging shall occur in water ranging from 0 to 5 parts per thousand salinity between
December 1 and June 30.
rows.normalized: The dredging operation shall not occur in water of 0-5 ppt salinity between December 1 and June 30.

rows.verbatim:
USACE shall implement a worker education program for listed fish species that could be
adversely impacted by dredging.
rows.normalized: USACE shall implement a worker education program for listed fish species impacted by dredging.

rows.verbatim:
The program shall include a presentation to all workers
on biology, general behavior, distribution and habitat needs, sensitivity to human
activities, legal protection status, and project-specific protective measures.
rows.normalized: The worker education program shall include a presentation to workers covering specified topics.

rows.verbatim:
Pump priming, drag head clearing, and suction of water at the beginning and end of
each hopper load shall be conducted within three feet of the seafloor.
rows.normalized: Pump priming, drag head clearing, and suction of water shall be conducted within three feet of the seafloor at the start/end of each hopper load.

rows.verbatim:
Hopper drag head suction pumps shall be turned off when raising and lowering the drag
arms from the seafloor.
rows.normalized: Hopper drag head suction pumps shall be turned off when raising and lowering the drag arms from the seafloor.

rows.verbatim:
The drag head, cutterheads, and pipeline intakes shall remain in contact with the
seafloor during suction dredging.
rows.normalized: The drag head, cutterheads, and pipeline intakes shall remain in contact with the seafloor during suction dredging.

rows.verbatim:
The drag head water intake doors shall be kept closed to the maximum extent
practicable in locations most vulnerable to entraining smelt.
rows.normalized: The drag head water intake doors shall be kept closed to the maximum extent practicable in locations vulnerable to entraining smelt.

rows.verbatim: In circumstances when the doors need to be opened to alleviate clogging, the doors shall be opened incrementally (i.e., the doors shall be opened in small increments and tested to see if the clog is removed) to ensure that doors are not fully opened unnecessarily.
rows.normalized: If drag head water intake doors need to be opened to alleviate clogging, the operator must open them incrementally and test to see if the clog is removed, ensuring doors are not fully opened unnecessarily.

rows.verbatim: Under all phases of the Project, hopper dredging will be conducted in accordance with the following hydraulic dredging standard practices included in the EA/EIR section 2.3.1.5 to avoid and minimize entrainment impacts to less than significant, including:
rows.normalized: Hopper dredging (contractor/executing party) will be conducted in accordance with the listed hydraulic dredging standard practices to avoid and minimize entrainment impacts.

rows.verbatim:
Should sediment characterization indicate elevated
contaminants, USACE is required in Provision 2 of this Order to implement additional z-layer4
characterization and/or practices to prevent resuspended sediment from spreading
contaminants, see Finding 6.
rows.normalized: If sediment characterization indicates elevated contaminants, USACE is required (per Provision 2) to implement additional z-layer characterization and/or practices to prevent contaminant spread.

rows.verbatim:
Leaking or overflow of scows are not permitted during
transport, preventing turbidity from increasing in route to sediment disposal or placement.
rows.normalized: Leaking or overflow of scows is not permitted during transport.

rows.verbatim:
Permitted discharges must comply with both the
federal and state antidegradation policies.
rows.normalized: Permitted discharges must comply with both federal and state antidegradation policies.

rows.verbatim:
IT IS HEREBY ORDERED, pursuant to the provisions of Division 7 of the California
Water Code and regulations adopted thereunder and other State regulations, as applicable, and
to the provisions of the federal Clean Water Act, as amended, and regulations and guidelines
adopted thereunder, that USACE shall comply with the following:
rows.normalized: USACE shall comply with the discharge prohibitions, limitations and provisions that follow.

rows.verbatim:
The discharge of water, material, or wastes that is not otherwise authorized by the Order
is prohibited.
rows.normalized: USACE must not discharge water, material, or wastes unless authorized by the Order.

rows.verbatim:
Dredging and disposal activities that create a condition of pollution or nuisance as
defined in section 13050(I) and (m) of the California Water Code are prohibited.
rows.normalized: USACE must not conduct dredging/disposal activities that create pollution or nuisance as defined by Water Code 13050(l),(m).

rows.verbatim:
Overflow, leakage, or spilling of dredged sediment from barges, bins or dump scows
during transportation from the dredging site to the placement site is prohibited.
rows.normalized: USACE must not allow overflow, leakage, or spilling of dredged sediment during transport from dredging to placement site.

rows.verbatim:
The discharge shall not cause a violation of any applicable water quality objectives for
receiving waters adopted by the Water Board and the State Water Board.
rows.normalized: USACE's discharge shall not violate applicable receiving water quality objectives.

rows.verbatim:
Maintenance dredging shall be implemented in conformance with the Project as
described in Finding 1 through 17 above, and all documents submitted with the
application for this Order.
rows.normalized: USACE shall implement maintenance dredging consistent with the Project description in Findings 1-17 and application documents.

rows.verbatim:
Should testing and analysis of the overlying sediment from the Project show
elevated levels of contaminants that may pose a threat to aquatic life, then
USACE shall include, in its episode approval request package, the best
management practices (BMPs) that will be used to prevent resuspended
sediment from leaving the Project area.
rows.normalized: If sediment testing shows elevated contaminants threatening aquatic life, USACE shall include BMPs in its episode approval request package.

rows.verbatim:
Should testing and analysis of the z-layer from the Project show elevated levels
of contaminants that may pose a threat to aquatic life, USACE shall coordinate
with the DMMO on a suitable plan, with a timeline, on actions and/or measures it
will implement to prevent exposure of the contaminated z-layer to aquatic life
post dredging.
rows.normalized: If z-layer testing shows elevated contaminants, USACE shall coordinate a timed plan with DMMO to prevent aquatic exposure post-dredging.

rows.verbatim:
This plan shall be coordinated before the episode approval request package is
submitted to the Water Board.
rows.normalized: USACE shall coordinate the z-layer plan before submitting the episode approval request package.

rows.verbatim:
USACE shall review the Programmatic EFH Conservation Measures for the LTMS Program Agreed-upon
by USACE, EPA, and NMFS dated June 9, 2011 for possible measures to
implement.
rows.normalized: USACE shall review the Programmatic EFH Conservation Measures (LTMS Program, June 9, 2011) for possible measures.

rows.verbatim:
All post-dredge and monitoring reports required by this Order shall be submitted to the
Water Board no later than June 30 each year through 2030, unless specified elsewhere
in this Order.
rows.normalized: USACE shall submit all post-dredge and monitoring reports to the Water Board no later than June 30 each year through 2030.

rows.verbatim:
As such, USACE is required to implement the following provisions as it applies to the different
areas of Project:
rows.normalized: USACE is required to implement the eelgrass-related provisions applicable to different Project areas.

rows.verbatim:
Consistent with the Programmatic Essential Fish Habitat Consultation Agreement
(Agreement), USACE shall conduct pre-dredge surveys of eelgrass areal
coverage and density within the dredge footprint where it overlaps the 250-meter
indirect impact buffer zone, conduct post-dredge surveys of eelgrass areal
coverage and density if eelgrass is present in the pre-dredge survey, and shall
send copies of these surveys to the Water Board; and
rows.normalized: USACE shall conduct pre- and post-dredge eelgrass surveys within the 250-meter buffer zone and send copies to the Water Board.

rows.verbatim:
Consistent with the Agreement, USACE shall implement light monitoring to protect eelgrass beds within 250 meters of dredging activity from adverse impacts due to excess turbidity in the water column and shall
send the Water Board the results of light monitoring studies.
rows.normalized: USACE shall implement light monitoring to protect eelgrass beds and send monitoring results to the Water Board.

rows.verbatim:
For each dredging episode, USACE shall coordinate the dredged sediment suitability
determinations through the DMMO, following applicable federal and state guidance on a
testing framework and on the preparation of reports.
rows.normalized: USACE shall coordinate sediment suitability determinations through DMMO for each dredging episode.

rows.verbatim:
USACE shall, as part of the episode approval
process, submit to the Water Board an evaluation of alternative disposal sites pursuant
to section 404(b)(1) of the Clean Water Act and the Dredge and Fill Procedures.
rows.normalized: USACE shall submit an alternative disposal sites evaluation (404(b)(1)) to the Water Board as part of the episode approval process.

rows.verbatim:
This type of evaluation, also known as an “Integrated Alternatives Analysis,” or IAA, shall
incorporate all USACE dredging projects (annual and non-annual) over as many
years/dredging cycles as possible, up to a maximum of five years, and shall evaluate the
practicability of the following beneficial reuse and disposal options:
rows.normalized: USACE's IAA shall incorporate all dredging projects for up to a maximum of five years and shall evaluate practicability of listed reuse/disposal options.

rows.verbatim:
USACE shall make good faith efforts to
coordinate with habitat restoration projects that are seeking dredged
sediment.
rows.normalized: USACE shall make good faith efforts to coordinate with habitat restoration projects seeking dredged sediment.

rows.verbatim:
USACE shall evaluate the practicability
of placing dredged sediment from the federal navigation channels at levee
restoration sites within the San Francisco Bay Region and USACE shall take
dredged sediment to those sites where it is practicable.
rows.normalized: USACE shall evaluate practicability of levee restoration reuse sites and take sediment there where practicable.

rows.verbatim:
USACE shall evaluate
the practicability of placing dredged sediment from the federal navigation
channels at other types of beneficial reuse sites and dredged sediment
rehandling sites within the San Francisco Bay Region and USACE shall take
dredged sediment to those sites where it is practicable.
rows.normalized: USACE shall evaluate practicability of other beneficial reuse/rehandling sites and take sediment there where practicable.

rows.verbatim:
USACE shall evaluate the
practicability of combining placement of dredged sediment from the federal
navigation channels with sediment from other USACE projects implementing
beneficial reuse when both projects will occur at similar times or locations or
will be performed by the same contractor.
rows.normalized: USACE shall evaluate practicability of combining sediment placement with other USACE beneficial reuse projects under specified conditions.

rows.verbatim: USACE shall submit the IAA by March 31, annually during years 2026 through 2029.
rows.normalized: USACE shall submit the Integrated Alternatives Analysis by March 31 annually, 2026-2029.

rows.verbatim:
Dredging episodes, including knockdown events, shall not
commence until authorized in writing by the Water Board Executive Officer.
rows.normalized: USACE's dredging episodes shall not commence until authorized in writing by the Water Board Executive Officer.

rows.verbatim:
At least 45
days prior to a dredging episode, USACE shall provide an episode approval request
package to the Water Board, with at least 30 days for the Water Board to review the
request.
rows.normalized: USACE shall provide an episode approval request package to the Water Board at least 45 days prior to a dredging episode.

rows.verbatim:
The package shall include the following
information specific to the episode:
rows.normalized: USACE's episode approval request package shall include the specified information.

rows.verbatim:
If testing and analysis of the overlying sediment in the Project show elevated
levels of contaminants that may pose a threat to aquatic life, include the BMPs
that will be used to prevent resuspended sediment from leaving the Project area
(include map of where BMPs will be implemented); and
rows.normalized: If overlying sediment testing shows elevated contaminants, USACE must include BMPs and a map in the episode package.

rows.verbatim:
If testing and analysis of the z-layer in the Project show elevated levels of
contaminants that may pose a threat to aquatic life, include a final plan, with
rows.normalized: If z-layer testing shows elevated contaminants, USACE must include a final plan (with timeline) in the episode package.

rows.verbatim:
The episode approval is dependent on the information provided in the request being
consistent with the certified and authorized Project in this Order, USACE’s most recent
IAA, and sediment suitability.
rows.normalized: USACE's episode approval depends on request information being consistent with the Order, most recent IAA, and sediment suitability.

rows.verbatim:
For each year covered by this Order, USACE shall
provide an electronic copy of a post-dredge report to the Water Board within 45 days
after all dredge projects funded in the same fiscal year have been completed, or by the
following June 30, whichever comes first.
rows.normalized: USACE shall provide an electronic post-dredge report to the Water Board within 45 days of fiscal-year project completion, or by June 30, whichever first.

rows.verbatim:
The post-dredge report for each channel shall be
submitted via email to RB2-Dredgereports@waterboards.ca.gov.
rows.normalized: USACE shall submit each channel's post-dredge report via email to RB2-Dredgereports@waterboards.ca.gov.

rows.verbatim:
The report shall contain the
following information:
rows.normalized: USACE's post-dredge report shall contain the listed information.

rows.verbatim:
When USACE implements Phase 1, documentation of the calculation to
determine the amount of mitigation needed to compensate for entrainment
impacts from hopper dredging, and the method of fulfilling this mitigation through
mitigation credits purchased or volume of sediment beneficial reused as
required in Provision 10.
rows.normalized: When USACE implements Phase 1, the report must document the mitigation calculation and fulfillment method per Provision 10.

rows.verbatim:
If USACE does not dredge a channel for which an episode approval was issued, it
shall provide a letter to the Water Board by February 14 the following year, specifying
which channel it did not dredge.
rows.normalized: If USACE does not dredge an approved channel, it shall notify the Water Board by letter by February 14 the following year.

rows.verbatim:
USACE shall provide a monitoring report that evaluates the water
quality impacts of the dredged sediment discharge on waters of the state.
rows.normalized: USACE shall provide a monitoring report evaluating water quality impacts of dredged sediment discharge.

rows.verbatim:
When implementing Phase 1, USACE shall compensate for unavoidable in-Bay hopper
dredging entrainment impacts by either: 1) purchasing longfin smelt mitigation credits at
a resource agency-approved habitat conservation bank, or 2) placing a volume of
dredged sediment at a non-aquatic beneficial reuse site for tidal wetland restoration, per
the equations below.
rows.normalized: When implementing Phase 1, USACE shall compensate for hopper dredging entrainment impacts via mitigation credits or beneficial reuse placement.

rows.verbatim:
If USACE complies by purchasing mitigation credits, the acres of mitigation required
shall be calculated using the following equation and the actual volume of water and
sediment pumped by the hopper dredge:
rows.normalized: If USACE purchases mitigation credits, the required acreage shall be calculated per the specified equation.

rows.verbatim:
If USACE complies by by placing a volume of dredged sediment at a non-aquatic
beneficial reuse site for tidal wetland restoration, the volume of dredged sediment shall
be determined using the following equation and the acres of mitigation calculated with
the previous equation:
rows.normalized: If USACE complies via non-aquatic beneficial reuse placement, the sediment volume shall be determined per the specified equation.

rows.verbatim:
USACE shall continue
monitoring to evaluate potential fish entrainment during hopper dredging by the USACE-owned ship, the Essayons, in the
San Francisco Bay as described in 2020-24 Monitoring Plan for Potential Fish
Entrainment During Dredging by The USACE Hopper Dredge Essayons in The San
Francisco Bay Area (updated 2023).
rows.normalized: USACE shall continue fish entrainment monitoring during hopper dredging per the 2020-24 Monitoring Plan.

rows.verbatim: Changes to this monitoring plan must be approved in writing by the Executive Officer.
rows.normalized: USACE must obtain written Executive Officer approval for changes to the monitoring plan.

rows.verbatim:
At a minimum USACE shall implement the following
monitoring techniques:
rows.normalized: USACE shall implement at least the listed monitoring techniques.

rows.verbatim:
An entrainment sampling apparatus shall sample dredged sediment that enters
through both drag arms by passing the dredged sediment slurry through a
rectangular shaped sieve.
rows.normalized: The entrainment sampling apparatus shall sample dredged sediment from both drag arms via a rectangular sieve.

rows.verbatim:
Biological Monitors (a lead delta smelt expert and three fisheries technician
assistants) shall conduct entrainment monitoring on a minimum of 80 percent of
the dredging passes from onboard the Essayons while the vessel dredges in the
San Francisco Bay.
rows.normalized: Biological Monitors shall conduct entrainment monitoring on a minimum of 80 percent of dredging passes aboard the Essayons.

rows.verbatim:
The biological monitors
shall sort, examine, and document the accumulated material in the sampling
apparatus.
rows.normalized: The biological monitors shall sort, examine, and document accumulated material in the sampling apparatus.

rows.verbatim:
Other opportunistic monitoring methods (e.g., observing water surface in the
hopper, sampling during water calibration and hopper flushing events) shall be
conducted when relevant opportunities arise.
rows.normalized: Other opportunistic monitoring methods shall be conducted when relevant opportunities arise.

rows.verbatim:
The annual entrainment monitoring report is due by June 30 of years 2026 through
2029.
rows.normalized: The annual entrainment monitoring report is due by June 30 of years 2026-2029.

rows.verbatim:
USACE shall notify the Water Board immediately by telephone and e-mail whenever an
adverse condition occurs due to the Project’s activities.
rows.normalized: USACE shall immediately notify the Water Board by phone and email whenever an adverse condition occurs.

rows.verbatim:
A written
notification of an adverse condition shall be submitted to the Water Board within 30 days
of occurrence, except that for petroleum products and hazardous substances
discharges, notification shall be to the California Office of Emergency Services as soon
as there is knowledge of the discharge and notification is possible without impeding
cleanup or emergency measures consistent with Water Code sections 13271 and
13272.
rows.normalized: USACE shall submit written notification of an adverse condition within 30 days of occurrence (or immediately to Cal OES for petroleum/hazardous substance discharges).

rows.verbatim:
The written notification shall identify the adverse condition, describe the action
necessary to remedy the condition, and specify a timetable, subject to the
modifications of the Water Board, for remedial actions.
rows.normalized: USACE's written notification shall identify the condition, describe remedial action, and specify a remedial timetable.

rows.verbatim:
In response to a suspected violation of any provision of this Order, the Water Board may
require USACE to furnish, under penalty of perjury, any technical or monitoring reports
the Water Board deems appropriate, under Water Code section 13383.
rows.normalized: If the Water Board suspects a violation, it may require USACE to furnish technical/monitoring reports under penalty of perjury.

rows.verbatim:
The discharge of dredged sediments to the waters of the State shall cease immediately
whenever violations of this Order are detected by USACE or by Water Board, and the
discharge shall not resume until compliance can be assured to the Executive Officer's
satisfaction.
rows.normalized: USACE's discharge shall cease immediately upon detected violations and shall not resume until compliance is assured to the Executive Officer.

rows.verbatim:
USACE shall provide the Water Board or its authorized representative, in accordance
with Water Code section 13267(c), with the following:
rows.normalized: USACE shall provide the Water Board or its representative with the listed access/records per Water Code 13267(c).

rows.verbatim:
USACE shall provide the Water Board or its authorized representative, in accordance
with Water Code section 13267(c), with the following:
a. Entry upon premises in which any required records are kept.
b. Access to copy any records required to be kept under terms and conditions of
this Order.
c. Access to inspect monitoring equipment required by this Order.
d. Access to sample any discharge.
e. Small craft transport to offshore locations or vessels for the purpose of
inspection, provided that it is within normal business hours.
rows.normalized: USACE must provide the Water Board or its representative with premises entry, record access, equipment inspection access, discharge sampling access, and small craft transport for inspection.

rows.verbatim:
The requirements of this Order must be met to ensure
that the Project will comply with water quality standards, any applicable effluent
limitations, standard of performance, prohibition, effluent standard, or pretreatment
standard requirement pursuant to the CWA above and to ensure that the Project will
comply with any other appropriate requirements of state law
rows.normalized: USACE must meet the Order's requirements to ensure Project compliance with CWA water quality standards and other state law requirements.

rows.verbatim:
Failure to implement the Project as proposed,
conditioned, and approved is a violation of this Order.
rows.normalized: Failing to implement the Project as proposed, conditioned, and approved constitutes a violation of the Order.

rows.verbatim: Dredging under this Order must be completed no later than May 15, 2030.
rows.normalized: USACE must complete dredging under this Order no later than May 15, 2030.

rows.verbatim: This Order expires on June 30, 2030.
rows.normalized: The Order expires on June 30, 2030.

rows.verbatim:
If the USACE does not agree with the conditions contained herein or fails to incorporate them into the
Program, the USACE shall notify the Commission immediately of its refusal to agree or to
incorporate the conditions into the Program or individual episodes and the conditional
concurrence shall be converted into an objection.
rows.normalized: If USACE disagrees with or fails to incorporate the conditions, USACE must immediately notify the Commission of its refusal.

rows.verbatim:
The USACE shall also notify the
Commission if the USACE determines to go forward with the Program or individual
project despite the Commission’s objection.
rows.normalized: USACE must notify the Commission if it decides to proceed with the Program despite the Commission's objection.

rows.verbatim:
Please sign the enclosed Letter of Agreement and return it to our offices within 10 days of
receipt.
rows.normalized: USACE must sign and return the enclosed Letter of Agreement within 10 days of receipt.
Dredge an average of 750,000 cy (up to 1,225,000 cy) annually from Oakland Inner/Outer Harbor to -50 ft MLLW plus 2 ft over-dredge, for four years.
Dredge an average of 300,000 cy (up to 630,000 cy) annually from Richmond Inner Harbor to -38 ft MLLW plus 2 ft over-dredge, for four years.
Dredge an average of 150,000 cy (up to 560,000 cy) annually from Pinole Shoal channel to -35 ft MLLW plus 2 ft over-dredge, for four years.
Dredge an average of 150,000 cy (up to 355,000 cy) annually from Suisun Bay channel to -35 ft MLLW plus 2 ft over-dredge, for four years.
Dredge an average of 180,000 cy (up to 650,000 cy) annually from Redwood City Harbor to -30 ft MLLW plus 2 ft over-dredge.
Dredge up to 30,000 cy from San Bruno Shoal to -30 ft MLLW plus 2 ft over-dredge, once during the four years.
Dredge up to 150,000 cy from the Petaluma River to -8 ft MLLW plus 2 ft over-dredge, once during four years.
Dredge up to 70,000 cy from Petaluma Across the Flats channel to -8 ft MLLW plus 2 ft over-dredge, once during four years.
Dredge up to 110,000 cy from the upper and lower Napa River channel to -9 ft MLLW plus 1 ft over-dredge, once during four years.
Dredge up to 110,000 cy from San Rafael Creek federal channel to -6 ft MLLW plus 2 ft over-dredge, once during four years.

rows.verbatim:
Conduct two “sea trials” of the federal hopper dredges, Essayons and/or Yaquina,
after dry dock repairs or maintenance activities between January and March in the
Pinole Shoal federal channel.
rows.normalized: Conduct two sea trials of the Essayons and/or Yaquina hopper dredges after dry dock repairs, between January and March, in the Pinole Shoal channel.

rows.verbatim:
Place
the dredged sediment at the state and federally authorized San Francisco Bar (SF-8)
disposal site, unless the sea state is prohibitive.
rows.normalized: Place sea-trial dredged sediment at the San Francisco Bar (SF-8) disposal site unless sea state is prohibitive.
If sea state is unsafe, dispose of sea-trial dredged sediment at San Pablo Bay (SF-10) or Alcatraz (SF-11) disposal site.

rows.verbatim:
Beneficially reuse dredged sediment from the federal navigation channels at
authorized beneficial reuse sites, or dispose of dredged sediment at the state and
federally authorized Alcatraz (SF-11), San Pablo Bay (SF-10), Carquinez Strait (SF-9),
and Suisun Bay (SF-16) disposal sites, or the San Francisco Deep Ocean Disposal Site
(SFDODS) in accord with the approved Integrated Alternative Disposal Site Analysis
(IAA) required in Special Condition II-C.

rows.verbatim: Dredging outside of the environmental work windows requires beneficial reuse of dredged sediment as mitigation for impacts to species.

rows.verbatim: If the USACE does not agree to comply with the following conditions or fails to incorporate them into its 2026-2029 Dredge Program, the USACE shall notify the Commission immediately of its refusal to agree or to incorporate any of the conditions into the Program, which would turn this conditional consistency determination concurrence into an objection.
rows.normalized: If USACE does not agree to or incorporate the special conditions, USACE shall immediately notify the Commission of its refusal.

rows.verbatim: The maximum volume authorized for shallow draft channels is 725,000 cy for 2026-2029.

rows.normalized: No dredging beyond authorized areas or volumes is permitted.

rows.verbatim: The USACE shall limit its in-Bay disposal volume to those shown in Tables 2 through 4 (Exhibit C), and work with the LTMS agencies through the Integrated Alternative Disposal Site Analysis (IAA) described in Special Condition II – C below.
rows.normalized: USACE shall limit in-Bay disposal volume to Tables 2-4 and coordinate with LTMS agencies via the IAA.

rows.normalized: USACE shall limit in-Bay disposal at each site to the monthly/annual limits in 14 CCR 10602(e)(1).

rows.verbatim: USACE will actively coordinate with the DMMO agencies to prevent breaches of in-Bay site limitations.
rows.normalized: USACE will actively coordinate with DMMO agencies to prevent breaches of in-Bay site limits.

rows.verbatim: Beginning in 2026, and no later than March 31st of each year, the USACE shall provide to the Commission an Integrated Alternative Disposal Site Analysis (IAA) for the year reflective of items 1 and 2 below, and its dredging schedule for the upcoming dredge season.
rows.normalized: USACE shall provide the Commission an annual IAA and dredge schedule no later than March 31 of each year beginning 2026.

rows.verbatim: By June 30th of any year, when necessary, USACE shall update the IAA to reflect changes in the USACE programming, funding, and equipment use and provide it to the Commission for review and approval.
rows.normalized: If necessary, USACE shall update and provide the IAA to the Commission by June 30 of that year.

rows.verbatim: The USACE shall include in its IAA all dredging projects (deep and shallow draft) for the calendar year, and as many as five years, the practicability of beneficial reuse of its dredged sediment at wetland restoration sites, levee maintenance, and other beneficial reuse opportunities, as well as disposal options, when beneficial reuse is not practicable.
rows.normalized: USACE shall include all dredging projects and beneficial reuse/disposal practicability analysis in its IAA.

rows.verbatim: To the extent such funds will be used, USACE will document it in the IAA including which projects and how much beneficial use will be achieved.
rows.normalized: If WRDA/SCC funds are used, USACE will document the projects and beneficial use achieved in the IAA.

rows.verbatim: The USACE shall maximize beneficial reuse of dredged sediment when practicable.
rows.normalized: USACE shall maximize beneficial reuse of dredged sediment when practicable.

rows.verbatim: The USACE shall evaluate the practicability of combining placement of dredged sediment from the federal navigation channels with sediment from other USACE projects implementing beneficial reuse when both projects will occur at similar times or locations or will be performed by the same contractor.
rows.normalized: USACE shall evaluate combining sediment placement with other beneficial-reuse projects under specified conditions.

rows.verbatim: Further, the USACE shall evaluate contracting mechanisms that ensure contractors include consideration of beneficial use in their bid proposals.
rows.normalized: USACE shall evaluate contracting mechanisms requiring contractors to consider beneficial use in bid proposals.

rows.verbatim: The dredge schedule should include all proposed projects for the calendar year and the estimated start and finish date, any projects anticipated to dredge outside of the environmental work windows, and the contracting schedule.
rows.normalized: The dredge schedule should include all projects, start/finish dates, out-of-window projects, and contracting schedule.

rows.verbatim: Should the USACE’s Dredging Program change, an updated schedule shall be provided to the Commission staff by June 30th of that same year.
rows.normalized: If the Dredging Program changes, an updated schedule shall be provided to the Commission by June 30 of that year.

rows.verbatim: By January 31, 2026, and prior to the commencement of any dredging episode authorized herein, the USACE shall submit to the Executive Director a water quality certification, waste discharge requirements, or any other required approvals from the California Regional Water Quality Control Board, San Francisco Bay Region (Water Board).
rows.normalized: USACE shall submit water quality certification/WDR approvals to the Executive Director by January 31, 2026 and before any dredging episode.

rows.verbatim: The USACE and/or its contractor shall immediately stop, repair, and clean up any fuel or hazardous waste leaks or spills from dredging or disposal activities at the time of occurrence.
rows.normalized: USACE and/or its contractor shall immediately stop, repair, and clean up fuel/hazardous waste spills at time of occurrence.

rows.verbatim: The USACE and/or its contractor shall properly contain hazardous products and dispose of any unused or leftover hazardous products outside of the Commission’s jurisdiction.
rows.normalized: USACE and/or its contractor shall properly contain and dispose of hazardous products outside the Commission's jurisdiction.

rows.verbatim: Sediment to be dredged, disposed, or beneficially reused shall be tested to ensure that it is physically, chemically and biologically suitable for the proposed disposal or beneficial reuse site.
rows.normalized: Sediment must be tested for physical/chemical/biological suitability before dredging, disposal, or beneficial reuse.

rows.verbatim: The sediment testing program shall be in accordance with the Inland Testing Manual or the Ocean Testing Manual, as modified for the San Francisco Bay Region,
rows.normalized: The sediment testing program shall follow the Inland or Ocean Testing Manual as modified for the SF Bay Region.

rows.normalized: Sampling and Analysis Plans and Result reports shall be submitted to DMMO two weeks before its meeting.

rows.verbatim: USACE shall submit SAPs that are consistent with the protocols, advice and decisions of the DMMO and include the proposed sample locations, the most recent survey of the channel, and both the dredge reaches and sample composite areas that are clear and legible.
rows.normalized: USACE shall submit SAPs consistent with DMMO protocols, including sample locations, recent survey, and clear/legible dredge reach and composite area maps.

rows.verbatim: USACE shall submit SARS in report form to the Commission staff and the DMMO for review and decision on the suitability of the sediment for the proposed disposal or placement site.
rows.normalized: USACE shall submit SARs in report form to Commission staff and DMMO for suitability review/decision.

rows.verbatim: The USACE shall abide by the decisions of the DMMO.
rows.normalized: USACE shall abide by DMMO decisions.
rows.section_ref: Special Condition E - Sampling Analysis Results (SAR)

rows.verbatim: At least 30 days prior to contract award, the USACE shall submit to the Commission’s Executive Director for review and approval the following information and documentation:
rows.normalized: USACE shall submit specified information/documentation to the Commission's Executive Director at least 30 days before contract award.
