rows.verbatim: A written statement shall be submitted to the Commission’s Executive Director with the following information: (1) the proposed disposal or placement site and quantity of sediment to be disposed or placed, and dates within which the disposal/placement episode is proposed; (2) if applicable, a discussion as to how the volume proposed for disposal is consistent with in-Bay disposal site limits and/or disposal site allocations; (3) the results of chemical and biological testing of sediment proposed for beneficial reuse or disposal; and (4) any changes to the IAA for the individual project, if any.
rows.normalized: A written statement with disposal site, quantity, dates, consistency discussion, test results, and IAA changes shall be submitted to the Executive Director.
rows.section_ref: Special Condition F.b Sediment Disposal and Placement

rows.verbatim: Within 15 days after the contract award, the USACE shall submit the latest bathymetric survey and written notification to the Commission that there are no changes to the project; or any revisions to the volume of sediment proposed for dredging, the disposal or placement site, and/or date of commencement from the initial submission.
rows.normalized: USACE shall submit the latest bathymetric survey and change/no-change notification to the Commission within 15 days after contract award.

rows.verbatim: The USACE shall adhere to any special conditions contained in the episode approval letter.
rows.normalized: USACE must adhere to special conditions in the episode approval letter.

rows.verbatim:
Within 60 days of the completion of all dredging projects funded in the same
federal fiscal year, or by June 30th of the following calendar year, the USACE shall
submit a signed post-bathymetric surveys to the Commission showing the actual
area(s) and depths dredged including over-dredge depth based on MLLW; any
dredging that occurred outside the authorized area or depths; the total volume of
sediment dredged, the placement or disposal location(s), and the volume of
sediment placed at each site; and the dates the dredging occurred.
rows.normalized: USACE must submit signed post-bathymetric surveys and dredging details to the Commission within 60 days of completion of all dredging projects in the same FY, or by June 30th of the following calendar year.

rows.verbatim:
Therefore, the USACE shall undertake the following avoidance, minimization, and
mitigation measures:
rows.normalized: USACE must undertake the listed avoidance, minimization, and mitigation measures.

rows.verbatim:
the USACE
shall confine dredging and in-Bay disposal operations to the work windows
consistent with Tables F-1 and F-2 of Appendix F, “In-Bay Disposal and Dredging”
and Figures 3.2 and 3.3 of the Long-Term Management Strategy (LTMS)
Management Plan (2001) programmatic biological opinions as amended by the U.S.
Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) on February 7, 2025 and NOAA’s National Marine
Fisheries Service (NMFS) in July 2015.
rows.normalized: USACE must confine dredging and in-Bay disposal operations to specified work windows per Appendix F tables and referenced biological opinions.

rows.verbatim:
If dredging is necessary outside the environmental work windows, the USACE shall
comply with the notification, monitoring, and conservation measures included in
the appropriate biological opinions and this Letter of Agreement.
rows.normalized: If dredging occurs outside environmental work windows, USACE must comply with notification, monitoring, and conservation measures from applicable biological opinions and the Agreement.

rows.verbatim:
No work inconsistent with the time and location limits contained in these figures
may be conducted without the written approval of an extension of time to
complete dredging and beneficial reuse and disposal by the Executive Director.
rows.normalized: No work inconsistent with the time/location limits may be conducted without the Executive Director's written approval of a time extension.

rows.verbatim:
Should the USACE obtain new or amended biological opinions that would change
the environmental work windows, the implementation of current biological
opinions, terms and conditions, or conservation measures, the USACE shall provide
them to the Commission for consideration.
rows.normalized: If USACE obtains new/amended biological opinions changing work windows or measures, USACE must provide them to the Commission for consideration.

rows.verbatim:
If the Commission determines that the new or amended biological opinion changes
the USACE Dredging Program in a way that is inconsistent with the Letter of
Agreement, the USACE shall work with the Commission staff to request and obtain
necessary amendments to this Letter of Agreement.
rows.normalized: If the Commission determines a new/amended biological opinion is inconsistent with the Agreement, USACE must work with Commission staff to obtain necessary amendments.

rows.verbatim:
No dredging (mechanical or hydraulic) is permitted from December 1 through May 31
upstream of, or within 1000 feet bayward of the mouths of Larkspur/Corte Madera
Creek, Napa River Channel/Mare Island Strait, Petaluma River, and Novato Creek
without the written approval of an extension of time to complete dredging and
beneficial reuse and disposal by the Executive Director.
rows.normalized: No mechanical or hydraulic dredging is permitted Dec 1-May 31 near listed tributary mouths without Executive Director written approval of a time extension.

rows.verbatim:
When circumstances necessitate that the USACE dredge before June 1st or after
November 30th anywhere in the Bay, to mitigate for impacts to Bay resources the
USACE shall place the sediment dredged after November 30th and before June 1st (or
August 1st for the Oakland Harbor Project) of any year at a designated beneficial reuse
site that will benefit fish habitat, consistent with the NMFS and USFWS amended LTMS
Programmatic Biological Opinions.
rows.normalized: If USACE dredges before June 1 or after November 30 anywhere in the Bay, USACE must place the sediment at a designated beneficial reuse site benefiting fish habitat, per amended LTMS Biological Opinions.

rows.verbatim:
This exemption does not apply to dredge sites upstream or within
1,000 feet bayward of the mouths of Larkspur/Corte Madera Creek, Napa
River Channel/Mare Island Strait, Petaluma River, and Novato Creek.
rows.normalized: The beneficial-reuse volume exemption does not apply to dredge sites near the listed tributary mouths.

rows.verbatim:
To protect native, state and federally listed, candidate, and species of special
concern, the USACE shall limit the use of a hydraulic dredge as follows:
rows.normalized: USACE must limit hydraulic dredge use per the following conditions to protect listed/special-concern species.

rows.verbatim:
No hydraulic dredging shall occur in Suisun Channel and clamshell dredging shall
be limited to the months of August 1st through November 30th of any year.
rows.normalized: No hydraulic dredging in Suisun Channel; clamshell dredging must be limited to Aug 1-Nov 30 annually.

rows.verbatim:
Hydraulic dredging in Pinole Shoal Channel shall be limited to the work window
of August 1st through November 30th of any year to protect listed species and
specifically to minimize impacts to longfin smelt and migrating salmonids.
rows.normalized: Hydraulic dredging in Pinole Shoal Channel must be limited to the Aug 1-Nov 30 work window annually.

rows.verbatim:
No hydraulic dredging shall occur at Richmond Outer Harbor from December 1st
to March 15th of any year to protect spawning herring, herring eggs, and larval
herring.
rows.normalized: No hydraulic dredging at Richmond Outer Harbor from Dec 1 to March 15 annually.

rows.verbatim:
Return water overflow from hopper-type hydraulic dredges shall be limited to no
longer than 15 minutes at the dredge site for each hopper load except in channels
where the shoaled material contains greater than 80 percent sand.
rows.normalized: Return water overflow from hopper dredges must be limited to no longer than 15 minutes per hopper load, except where shoaled material exceeds 80% sand.

rows.verbatim:
To reduce entrainment of fish and invertebrates, the USACE shall implement the
following minimization measures when using a hydraulic dredge:
rows.normalized: USACE must implement the listed minimization measures when using a hydraulic dredge.

rows.verbatim:
The USACE shall designate a qualified biologist to provide a worker education
and training program regarding special status fish species that could be adversely
impacted by dredging.
rows.normalized: USACE must designate a qualified biologist to provide a worker education/training program on special status fish species.

rows.verbatim:
The training program shall be conducted prior to the use of a hydraulic dredge in
San Francisco Bay.
rows.normalized: The worker training program must be conducted prior to hydraulic dredge use in San Francisco Bay.

rows.verbatim: In addition, the following measures shall be implemented:
rows.normalized: The following drag head operation measures must be implemented.

rows.verbatim:
(1) Suction pumps shall be turned off when raising and lowering the drag arms
from the seafloor;
rows.normalized: Suction pumps must be turned off when raising/lowering drag arms from the seafloor.

rows.verbatim:
(2) The drag head or cutter head shall maintain contact with the seafloor during
dredging; and
rows.normalized: The drag head or cutter head must maintain contact with the seafloor during dredging.

rows.verbatim: (3) Opening water intake doors on the drag head shall be minimized.
rows.normalized: Opening of water intake doors on the drag head must be minimized.

rows.verbatim:
When necessary to alleviate clogging, the doors shall be opened incrementally, (i.e.,
the doors shall be opened in small increments and tested to see if the clog is
removed) to ensure that doors are not fully opened unnecessarily.
rows.normalized: If clogging must be alleviated, doors must be opened incrementally and tested rather than fully opened.

rows.verbatim:
To better understand the entrainment rate and the impact of hydraulic dredging on
native and listed species, the USACE shall:
rows.normalized: USACE must perform the following entrainment monitoring actions.

rows.verbatim:
By March 31, 2026, USACE shall submit a four-year entrainment monitoring plan,
acceptable to the Executive Director, that describes the collection and recording
of entrainment of native and listed fish and macroinvertebrate species.
rows.normalized: USACE must submit a four-year entrainment monitoring plan acceptable to the Executive Director by March 31, 2026.
The entrainment monitoring plan must, at a minimum, include the seven listed elements (a)-(g).

rows.verbatim:
Annual monitoring reports containing the above-described information along
with any proposed updates to the monitoring plan shall be submitted to the
Commission by January 31st of the year following the dredging and monitoring
activities.
rows.normalized: Annual monitoring reports and proposed plan updates must be submitted to the Commission by January 31 of the year following dredging/monitoring activities.

rows.verbatim:
The USACE shall report any special status species and natural communities
detected during the entrainment monitoring to the California Natural
Diversity Database (CNDDB).
rows.normalized: USACE must report any special status species/natural communities detected during entrainment monitoring to the CNDDB.

rows.verbatim:
When the USACE uses a hydraulic dredge, it shall compensate for unavoidable take of native and listed species via entrainment by:
a. purchasing longfin smelt mitigation credits at a resource agency-approved
habitat conservation bank; and/or
b. by beneficially reusing a volume of dredged sediment at a wetland restoration
project that benefits fish habitat.
rows.normalized: When USACE uses a hydraulic dredge, USACE must compensate for entrainment take of native/listed species via mitigation credits and/or beneficial reuse of dredged sediment.
rows.section_ref: Mitigation for Entrainment of Native and Listed Species

rows.verbatim:
To calculate acreage of mitigation credits needed the USACE shall use the actual
volume of water and sediment pumped by the hopper dredge in the equation
below:
rows.normalized: USACE must use the actual volume of water/sediment pumped by the hopper dredge in the specified equation to calculate mitigation acreage.
rows.section_ref: Mitigation for Entrainment of Native and Listed Species

rows.verbatim:
To calculate the volume of dredged sediment required for beneficial reuse the
USACE shall use the following equation and the acres of mitigation calculated with
the previous equation:
rows.normalized: USACE must use the specified equation to calculate volume of dredged sediment required for beneficial reuse.
rows.section_ref: Mitigation for Entrainment of Native and Listed Species

rows.verbatim:
After implementing this mitigation requirement for three dredging seasons,
the USACE shall compile the amount of sediment dredged using hydraulic
dredges; the amount of water pumped through the system; the amount and
typed of fish and macro invertebrates entrained; the amount of sediment
beneficially reused; and the amount of wetlands (acres) restored as a result
of this mitigation requirement.
rows.normalized: After three dredging seasons of mitigation implementation, USACE must compile data on sediment dredged, water pumped, species entrained, sediment reused, and wetlands restored.

rows.verbatim:
A three-year report shall be provided to the
Commission by July 31, 2029 for review and consideration in its next
evaluation of any future USACE hydraulic Dredging Program.
rows.normalized: USACE must provide a three-year report to the Commission by July 31, 2029.

rows.verbatim:
If the determination is made by the Commission or resources agencies that
the mitigation provided is not sufficient to offset the impacts of the hydraulic
dredging, a more appropriate mitigation program shall be developed for
consideration of future authorization of future hydraulic dredging.
rows.normalized: If the Commission or resource agencies determine mitigation is insufficient, a more appropriate mitigation program must be developed.

rows.verbatim:
When the USACE uses a hydraulic dredge, it shall compensate for unavoidable take
of native and listed species via entrainment by:
rows.normalized: When USACE uses a hydraulic dredge, it must compensate for unavoidable entrainment take of native/listed species by the listed methods.

rows.verbatim:
The USACE is required, as prescribed in the State and Federal Endangered Species Acts, to consult with or obtain appropriate take
authorization from the appropriate agencies prior to undertaking dredging activities
in San Francisco Bay which may affect any federally or state listed species and is not
rows.normalized: USACE is required to consult with or obtain take authorization from appropriate agencies prior to dredging activities affecting listed species, per Endangered Species Acts.

rows.verbatim:
If the USACE initiates consultation with one or more resource agencies, it shall
provide a copy of the amended or new biological opinion to the Commission staff for
consideration and potential amendment to this Letter of Agreement as required by
the Commission.
rows.normalized: If USACE initiates consultation with resource agencies, USACE must provide a copy of the amended/new biological opinion to the Commission staff.

rows.verbatim:
The USACE shall use the appropriate protocols, as approved by the CDFW, NMFS, and/or USFWS, to ensure that project activities do not adversely
affect rare, candidate, threatened and endangered species, as they are protected
natural resources of San Francisco Bay and its tributaries.
rows.normalized: USACE must use approved protocols to ensure project activities do not adversely affect protected species.

rows.verbatim:
Should it become necessary to dredge within herring spawning habitat and outside of the herring work window (March 16th to November 30th of any year), the USACE shall implement the
following measures:
rows.normalized: If dredging within herring spawning habitat outside the work window becomes necessary, USACE must implement the listed measures.

rows.verbatim:
A CDFW qualified and trained herring observer shall be present during all dredging
or in-water work (day and night) and observing shall be his/her sole duty.
rows.normalized: A CDFW-qualified herring observer must be present during all dredging/in-water work, with observing as sole duty.

rows.verbatim:
The herring observer shall monitor for herring spawn in 500-meter buffer zone
surrounding active dredging and disposal activities.
rows.normalized: The herring observer must monitor for herring spawn within a 500-meter buffer zone around dredging/disposal activities.
Observations must have a full view of the buffer zone, whether conducted from dredge, shore, or vessel.
If there is a lag of eight or more hours between dredging activities, the herring observer must conduct a shoreline survey at least one hour before dredging resumes.

rows.verbatim:
If spawning Pacific herring are detected within 500 meters of the dredging site all in-
water work shall stop immediately and Commission staff and CDFW shall be notified.
rows.normalized: If spawning herring are detected within 500 meters, all in-water work must stop immediately and Commission staff/CDFW must be notified.

rows.verbatim:
If spawning occurs within the 500-meter buffer, work may not continue until spawning
has ended and herring embryos have hatched (14-21 days).
rows.normalized: If spawning occurs within the buffer, work must not continue until spawning ends and embryos hatch (14-21 days).

rows.verbatim: Dredging can restart with approval from CDFW and notification to the Commission staff;
rows.normalized: Dredging may restart only with CDFW approval and notification to the Commission staff.

rows.verbatim:
The observer shall keep a daily log of observations, which shall be submitted to
Commission staff and the CDFW on a weekly basis by 5:00 pm on Fridays; and
rows.normalized: The observer must keep a daily log and submit it weekly to Commission staff and CDFW by 5:00 pm on Fridays.

rows.verbatim:
For Oakland and Richmond Inner Harbor dredging conducted outside the herring work
window, the dredging contractor shall dredge the remaining sediment moving to the
outer reaches and work towards the inner harbor to reduce disturbance to spawning
activity.
rows.normalized: For Oakland/Richmond Inner Harbor dredging outside the herring work window, the dredging contractor must dredge from outer reaches toward the inner harbor.

rows.verbatim: observing shall be his/her sole duty.
rows.normalized: The herring observer must have observing dredging/in-water work as his/her sole duty.

rows.verbatim: Commission staff and CDFW shall be notified.
rows.normalized: If spawning Pacific herring are detected within 500 meters of the dredging site, Commission staff and CDFW shall be notified.

rows.verbatim: which shall be submitted to Commission staff and the CDFW on a weekly basis by 5:00 pm on Fridays
rows.normalized: The observer shall submit the daily log of observations to Commission staff and CDFW weekly by 5:00 pm on Fridays.

rows.verbatim:
Due to the presence of eelgrass beds in the vicinity of the
Richmond and Oakland Harbor federal navigation channels, the USACE shall
implement the USACE SF Bay Dredging Program Eelgrass Light Monitoring Plan
2024-2030 (Light Monitoring Plan), including turbidity minimization measures
described in Table 1, Page 14 of the Light Monitoring Plan.
rows.normalized: USACE must implement the Eelgrass Light Monitoring Plan 2024-2030, including turbidity minimization measures.

rows.verbatim:
With 60 days of completion of the post dredge eelgrass survey, the USACE shall
provide a copy of the light monitoring report, inclusive of the pre-dredge and
post dredge eelgrass surveys, and an analysis of any changes to the eelgrass beds
within 250 meters of dredging activity.
rows.normalized: Within 60 days of completing the post-dredge eelgrass survey, USACE must provide the light monitoring report and analysis to the Commission.

rows.verbatim:
Should the USACE determine it is necessary to alter the Light Monitoring Plan, it
shall provide proposed changes to the Commission for review and approval 30
days prior to implementing changes.
rows.normalized: If USACE decides to alter the Light Monitoring Plan, it must provide proposed changes to the Commission for review 30 days before implementation.

rows.verbatim:
The USACE shall maintain administrative controls on disposal volumes at the in-Bay
disposal sites to ensure that LTMS in-Bay disposal volume and the in-Bay disposal sites
specific volumes are not exceeded.
rows.normalized: USACE must maintain administrative controls on disposal volumes to ensure LTMS and site-specific volume limits are not exceeded.
rows.section_ref: J. Management and Monitoring of In-Bay Disposal Sites

rows.verbatim:
The USACE shall manage overall disposal volumes
and disposal locations within each site in coordination with the LTMS agencies to
prevent build-up of dredged materials at each of the sites.
rows.normalized: USACE must manage disposal volumes/locations in coordination with LTMS agencies to prevent material build-up.
rows.section_ref: J. Management and Monitoring of In-Bay Disposal Sites

rows.verbatim:
The USACE shall continue bathymetric monitoring of the in-Bay disposal sites,
monthly at SF-11, quarterly at SF-9, SF-10, and SF-16.
rows.normalized: USACE must continue bathymetric monitoring: monthly at SF-11 and quarterly at SF-9, SF-10, SF-16.
rows.section_ref: J. Management and Monitoring of In-Bay Disposal Sites

rows.verbatim:
The USACE shall provide these condition surveys within 60 days of their
completion to the Commission staff.
rows.normalized: USACE must provide condition surveys to the Commission staff within 60 days of completion.
rows.section_ref: J. Management and Monitoring of In-Bay Disposal Sites

rows.verbatim:
Upon request of the LTMS agencies, the USACE shall provide analysis of the
condition of the in-Bay disposal sites.
rows.normalized: Upon request of LTMS agencies, USACE must provide analysis of the condition of in-Bay disposal sites.
rows.section_ref: J. Management and Monitoring of In-Bay Disposal Sites

rows.verbatim:
Beginning in 2027, and by March 31st of each year, the USACE shall brief the Commission
at one of its regularly scheduled meetings on the outcome of the implementation of the
Dredging Program for the previous year.
rows.normalized: Beginning 2027, USACE must brief the Commission by March 31st each year on the prior year's Dredging Program implementation.

rows.verbatim:
The briefing shall
include information and documentation on the amount of sediment dredged and beneficially
reused, the volume of sediment disposed of, where the sediment was beneficially reused or
disposed, the work completed in and out of the work window, the amount of mitigation
required and implemented, the acres of habitat created through mitigation, and the funding
that was available and was used for beneficial reuse of the USACE dredged sediment.
rows.normalized: The annual briefing must include specified data on sediment dredged, reused, disposed, mitigation, habitat, and funding.

rows.verbatim:
The USACE shall allow the Commission staff and representatives of other relevant state or
federal agencies to come aboard the dredge or barge associated with any dredging or
disposal episode and observe the operation(s) to ensure that these activities are
consistent with the terms and conditions of this Letter of Agreement.
rows.normalized: USACE must allow Commission and relevant agency staff to board dredges/barges to observe operations for consistency with the Agreement.
rows.section_ref: L. Observation of Dredging and Disposal Operations

rows.verbatim:
If, at any time during the effective life of this Letter of Agreement, the Commission's
laws, Bay Plan policies, or regulations are changed and are in effect as enforceable
policies of the Commission's certified coastal management program under the federal
Coastal Zone Management Act regarding dredging, dredged sediment disposal, and
beneficial reuse, this Letter of Agreement shall become null and void unless the USACE
agrees to amend its consistency determination, and agrees to new conditions to meet
the new laws, policies, or regulations in a manner specified by or on behalf of the
Commission, if appropriate.
rows.normalized: If Commission laws/policies/regulations change during the Agreement's life, the Agreement becomes null and void unless USACE agrees to amend its consistency determination and meet new conditions.
rows.section_ref: M. Changes to Commission Laws, Policies, and Regulations

rows.verbatim: The USACE has offered minimization measures for hydraulic dredging, which are required in Special Condition II – H.3.
rows.normalized: USACE is required to implement hydraulic dredging minimization measures per Special Condition II-H.3.

rows.verbatim: “The USACE will dispose of dredged material according to the LTMS work windows, which were established in coordination with the USFWS, NMFS, and CDFW.
rows.normalized: USACE will dispose of dredged material according to the LTMS work windows established with USFWS, NMFS, and CDFW.

rows.verbatim: Special Condition II – G is included to require the mitigation through beneficial reuse but allows for the USACE to complete the mitigation before dredging outside the work window, and/or provide the mitigation in the following dredge season.
rows.normalized: USACE must complete mitigation through beneficial reuse before dredging outside the work window, or provide it in the following dredge season, per Special Condition II-G.

rows.verbatim: Special Condition II – H.1, limits hydraulic dredging in channels within spawning areas to times of the year that spawning is not occurring.
rows.normalized: USACE's hydraulic dredging in spawning-area channels is limited to times when spawning is not occurring, per Special Condition II-H.1.

rows.verbatim: the Commission has included Special Condition II-H.1. restrict hydraulic dredging during the herring spawning season in Richmond and Oakland federal navigation channels.
rows.normalized: Hydraulic dredging is restricted during herring spawning season in Richmond and Oakland federal navigation channels per Special Condition II-H.1.

rows.verbatim: Dredging Policy 1 states that dredgers shall collectively reduce disposal in the Bay and certain waterways over time to a maximum of one million cubic yards per year as described in the LTMS program
rows.normalized: Dredgers must collectively reduce Bay disposal over time to a maximum of one million cubic yards per year, per Dredging Policy 1.

rows.verbatim: Special Condition II – C requires the USACE to provide an annual integrated alternative disposal site analysis to the Commission by March 31st of each year for review and approval.
rows.normalized: USACE must provide an annual integrated alternative disposal site analysis to the Commission by March 31st of each year for review and approval.

rows.verbatim: Special Condition II – K requires the USACE to provide an annual briefing to the Commission regarding how it is meeting the goals of maximally beneficially reusing sediment and includes specific criteria for this report.
rows.normalized: USACE must provide an annual briefing to the Commission on meeting beneficial reuse goals, per specific criteria required in Special Condition II-K.

rows.verbatim: Special Conditions II – E and F require information regarding the sediment quality be submitted to the Commission for review and approval prior to each dredging episode to ensure that water quality and habitat quality is protected.
rows.normalized: USACE must submit sediment quality information to the Commission for review and approval prior to each dredging episode.

rows.verbatim: “Sediment will be dredged using mechanical and hydraulic methods and is proposed for placement at various sites, in compliance with the Long-Term Management Strategy (LTMS) and other applicable regional sediment management goals.”
rows.normalized: USACE will dredge sediment using mechanical and hydraulic methods and place it at various sites in compliance with LTMS and other regional sediment management goals.

rows.verbatim: Special Condition II – G requires the dredging within the work window and a process for evaluating time extensions to the windows, consistent with the resources agencies decisions.
rows.normalized: USACE is required to dredge within the designated work window and follow a process for evaluating time extensions to the windows.

rows.verbatim: Special Condition II – H limits the timing and location of hydraulic dredging in areas of the Bay that are important spawning habitat for Pacific herring, longfin and Delta smelt.
rows.normalized: USACE's hydraulic dredging timing and location is limited in Bay areas that are important spawning habitat for Pacific herring, longfin and Delta smelt.

rows.verbatim: Special Condition II – H.5 requires the use of an equation to calculate the amount of mitigation credits that would be provided if an appropriate mitigation bank is available.
rows.normalized: USACE is required to use an equation to calculate mitigation credits if an appropriate mitigation bank is available.

rows.verbatim: Special Condition II – H.6 requires an analysis of the effectiveness of the mitigation strategy be provided to the Commission after 3 years of program implementation to assist in determining whether the strategy is working or should be revised in future hydraulic Dredging Programming.
rows.normalized: USACE is required to provide the Commission an analysis of the mitigation strategy's effectiveness after 3 years of program implementation.

rows.verbatim: Should either of these agencies require additional mitigation, the USACE shall comply with those requirements.
rows.normalized: If NMFS or USFWS require additional mitigation, USACE shall comply with those requirements.

rows.verbatim: This Letter of Agreement shall not take effect unless the USACE executes the original of this Letter of Agreement and returns it to the Commission within ten days after the date of the issuance of the Letter of Agreement.
rows.normalized: USACE must execute and return the original Letter of Agreement to the Commission within ten days after its issuance date for it to take effect.

rows.verbatim: No work shall be done until the acknowledgment is duly executed and returned to the Commission.
rows.normalized: USACE shall not begin work until the acknowledgment is executed and returned to the Commission.

rows.verbatim: All required permissions from governmental bodies must be obtained before the commencement of work; these bodies include, but are not limited to, the U. S. Army Corps of Engineers, the Regional Water Quality Control Board, and the city or county in which the work is to be performed, whenever any of these may be required.
rows.normalized: USACE must obtain all required governmental permissions before commencing work.

rows.verbatim: Work must be performed in the precise manner and at the precise locations indicated in USACE’s consistency determination request, as may have been modified by the terms of the Letter of Agreement and any plans approved in writing by or on behalf of the Commission.
rows.normalized: USACE must perform work exactly as indicated in its consistency determination request, as modified by the LOA or Commission-approved plans.

rows.verbatim: The USACE shall grant permission to any member of the Commission’s staff to conduct a site visit at the subject properties during and after performance of work to verify that the project is being and has been performed in compliance with the authorization and conditions contained herein.
rows.normalized: USACE shall grant Commission staff permission to conduct site visits during and after work performance.

rows.verbatim: All debris shall be removed to an authorized location outside the jurisdiction of the Commission.
rows.normalized: USACE/contractor shall remove all debris to an authorized location outside the Commission's jurisdiction.

rows.verbatim: In the event that any such material is placed in any area within the Commission's jurisdiction, the USACE or their contractors shall remove such material, at their expense, within ten days after they have been notified by the Executive Director of such placement.
rows.normalized: If debris is placed within the Commission's jurisdiction, USACE or its contractors shall remove it at their own expense within ten days of notification by the Executive Director.

rows.verbatim:
Unless otherwise provided in this Letter of Agreement, all the terms and conditions of
this Letter of Agreement shall remain effective for so long as the Letter of Agreement
remains in effect.
rows.normalized: Unless otherwise provided, all terms and conditions of the Letter of Agreement shall remain effective for as long as the Letter of Agreement is in effect.

rows.verbatim: All construction operations shall be performed to prevent construction materials from falling, washing or blowing into the Bay.
rows.normalized: Construction operations shall be performed to prevent materials from falling, washing, or blowing into the Bay.

rows.verbatim: In the event that such material escapes or is placed in an area subject to tidal action of the Bay, USACE or its contractors shall immediately retrieve and remove such material at their expense.
rows.normalized: If material escapes into the Bay's tidal area, USACE or its contractors shall immediately retrieve and remove it at their expense.

rows.verbatim: Dredge permit applicants must submit to the DMMO a SAP to confirm the suitability of sediment proposed to be dredged for unconfined aquatic placement in-Bay or at San Francisco Deep Ocean Disposal Site (SF-DODS), or upland/beneficial reuse placement.
rows.normalized: Dredge permit applicants (possibly including the contractor) must submit a SAP to the DMMO confirming sediment suitability for the proposed placement/disposal method.

rows.verbatim: Sediment testing and analysis must be implemented as approved in the SAP and the results presented to the DMMO.
rows.normalized: The party conducting sediment testing must implement testing/analysis as approved in the SAP and present results to the DMMO.

rows.verbatim: Corps conducted or funded dredging of federal navigation channels will be performed in compliance with these measures.
rows.normalized: Contractor-performed dredging of federal navigation channels must comply with the specified avoidance/minimization/mitigation measures.

rows.verbatim:
No dredging (mechanical or hydraulic) will be permitted from December 1 through May
31 upstream or within 1000 feet bayward of the mouths of Larkspur/Corte Madera Creek, Napa River Channel/Mare Island Strait (including Vallejo), Petaluma River, and Novato Creek without individual consultation.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall not conduct mechanical or hydraulic dredging Dec 1 - May 31 upstream/within 1000 ft of specified creek mouths without individual consultation.

rows.verbatim: If a project is unable to place all of the material dredged outside the work window at a beneficial reuse site (e.g., due to equipment constraints or site availability), absent additional consultation, the project proponent will be required to provide an equivalent volume of material, deemed suitable for the purpose by DMMO, to a similar beneficial reuse site from a dredging project conducted inside the work window (June 1 to November 30) and not otherwise planned to go to a reuse site benefitting aquatic habitat.
rows.normalized: If a project cannot place all out-of-window dredged material at a beneficial reuse site, the project proponent must provide an equivalent volume of suitable material to a similar beneficial reuse site from a within-window project, absent additional consultation.

rows.verbatim: The placement of a like volume of dredged material at a beneficial reuse site must occur within 12 months of the end of the previous work window (i.e. November 30th).
rows.normalized: Contractor/project proponent must place the equivalent replacement volume of dredged material at a beneficial reuse site within 12 months of the end of the prior work window.

rows.verbatim:
Dredging at each project location will continue to be limited to the approved
project depth plus over-depth.
rows.normalized: Contractor must limit dredging at each project location to the approved project depth plus over-depth.

rows.verbatim:
No overflow or decant water will be allowed to be discharged from any barge,
with the exception of spillage incidental to clamshell dredge operations,
unless monitoring or relevant studies show the effects of such discharge are
negligible on water quality.
rows.normalized: Contractor must not discharge overflow or decant water from any barge, except incidental clamshell spillage or where studies show negligible water quality effects.

rows.verbatim:
To reduce turbidity that may affect fish habitat, return water overflow from
hopper-type suction dredges would continue to be limited to no longer than
15 minutes at the dredge site during any one excavation action (cut).
rows.normalized: Contractor must limit return water overflow from hopper-type suction dredges to no longer than 15 minutes per excavation action (cut).

rows.verbatim:
Overflow would be unrestricted when dredged material is greater than 90
percent sand.
rows.normalized: If dredged material is greater than 90 percent sand, the overflow time limit does not apply.

rows.verbatim:
Turbidity control and/or monitoring measures will be required per the
provisions of the LTMS Programmatic EFH Agreement when dredging occurs
in proximity to identified eelgrass zones.
rows.normalized: If dredging occurs near identified eelgrass zones, contractor must implement turbidity control and/or monitoring measures per the LTMS Programmatic EFH Agreement.

rows.verbatim:
Mitigation for any direct loss of eelgrass due to dredging will occur in
consultation with NMFS, per the provisions of the LTMS Programmatic EFH
Agreement.
rows.normalized: For any direct loss of eelgrass due to dredging, mitigation must occur in consultation with NMFS per the LTMS Programmatic EFH Agreement.

rows.verbatim:
Monthly and annual disposal volume limits will remain in place for each in-
Bay disposal site.
rows.normalized: Contractor's disposal volumes must remain within the monthly and annual limits set for each in-Bay disposal site.

rows.verbatim:
Where applicable, projects must be conducted in accordance with an
Alternatives Analyses or Integrated Alternatives Analysis approved by the
LTMS agencies, to demonstrate that they are meeting the LTMS in-Bay
disposal goals to the extent practicable and feasible.
rows.normalized: Where applicable, the contractor must conduct projects in accordance with an approved Alternatives Analysis or Integrated Alternatives Analysis demonstrating compliance with LTMS in-Bay disposal goals.

rows.verbatim:
For hopper or pipeline dredging projects, a worker education program will be
implemented for listed fish that could be adversely impacted by dredging.
rows.normalized: For hopper or pipeline dredging projects, contractor must implement a worker education program regarding listed fish that could be adversely impacted by dredging.

rows.verbatim:
Workers would also be
provided with written materials containing this information.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide workers with written materials containing the education program information.

rows.verbatim:
Draghead or pipeline pumps will only be turned on when the dragheads, cutterheads,
or pipeline intakes are on the seafloor or within 3 feet of the seafloor when priming
pumps.
rows.normalized: Contractor must only turn on draghead or pipeline pumps when dragheads/cutterheads/pipeline intakes are on or within 3 feet of the seafloor during priming.

rows.verbatim:
Draghead, cutterheads, or pipeline intakes will be monitored so that they
maintain positive contact with the seafloor during suction dredging.
rows.normalized: Contractor must monitor dragheads, cutterheads, or pipeline intakes to maintain positive contact with the seafloor during suction dredging.

rows.verbatim:
Hopper dredges will close, to the extent possible, the draghead water intake port's
doors in locations most vulnerable to entraining or entrapping listed fish.
rows.normalized: Contractor must close hopper dredge draghead water intake port doors, to the extent possible, in locations most vulnerable to entraining/entrapping listed fish.

rows.verbatim: Planned LTMS dredging projects that are performed outside of the work windows for listed anadromous salmonids (June 1 through November 30) are required by the LTMS Program to placed dredged materials at a beneficial reuse site that will provide future aquatic habitat benefits for San Francisco Bay native species.
rows.normalized: LTMS dredging projects performed outside the June 1–November 30 work window must place dredged materials at a beneficial reuse site that provides future aquatic habitat benefits for San Francisco Bay native species.

rows.verbatim: Future dredging and disposal of dredged materials conducted under the LTMS Program and addressed by this biological opinion must be conducted in compliance with the following programmatic measures:
rows.normalized: Contractor must conduct future LTMS dredging and disposal in compliance with the listed programmatic measures.

rows.verbatim: (1) The work window for dredging and disposal is June 1 through November 30.
rows.normalized: Dredging and disposal work window is limited to June 1 through November 30.

rows.verbatim: (2) No dredging will be permitted from December 1 through May 31 upstream or within 1000 feet bayward of the mouths of Larkspur/Corte Madera Creek, Napa River Channel/Mare Island Strait, Petaluma River, and Novato Creek.
rows.normalized: Contractor must not dredge from December 1 through May 31 upstream or within 1000 feet bayward of the mouths of Larkspur/Corte Madera Creek, Napa River Channel/Mare Island Strait, Petaluma River, and Novato Creek.

rows.verbatim: (3) Projects may plan work for the period outside the work window (December 1 through May 31) provided the project mitigates for its impacts by placing dredged material at a beneficial re-use site, such as tidal wetlands restoration site.
rows.normalized: If a project plans work outside the work window (December 1–May 31), it must mitigate impacts by placing dredged material at a beneficial re-use site such as a tidal wetlands restoration site.

rows.verbatim: This exemption does not apply to dredge sites upstream or within 1000 feet bayward of the mouths of Larkspur/Corte Madera Creek, Napa River Channel/Mare Island Strait, Petaluma River, and Novato Creek.
rows.normalized: The equivalent-volume exemption for out-of-window dredging does not apply to dredge sites upstream or within 1000 feet bayward of the mouths of Larkspur/Corte Madera Creek, Napa River Channel/Mare Island Strait, Petaluma River, and Novato Creek.

rows.verbatim: Best management practices that require pumps to be turned on only when the intake is within three feet of the seafloor are expected to reduce the risk of listed fish from being entrained.
rows.normalized: Contractor's best management practices require dredge pumps to be turned on only when the intake is within three feet of the seafloor.

rows.verbatim:
Dredging and disposal of dredged materials conducted or funded (in whole or in part) by the
USACE must adhere to all appropriate LTMS Program measures and best management
practices, including the following:
rows.normalized: Dredging and disposal activities conducted or funded by USACE must adhere to all applicable LTMS Program measures and best management practices listed.

rows.verbatim:
No dredging will be permitted from December 1 through May 31 upstream or
within 1,000 feet bayward of the mouths of Larkspur/Corte Madera Creek, Napa
River Channel/Mare Island Strait, Petaluma River, and Novato Creek.
rows.normalized: No dredging is permitted from December 1 through May 31 upstream or within 1,000 feet bayward of the specified creek mouths.

rows.verbatim:
Cutterhead dredges shall not be turned on until the suction dredge head is submerged in the
sediment to minimize potential for entrainment of fish in the water column.
rows.normalized: Cutterhead dredges shall not be turned on until the suction dredge head is submerged in sediment.

rows.verbatim:
Knockdowns are subject to the same sediment testing requirements and approvals as full
dredging episodes.
rows.normalized: Knockdown operations must meet the same sediment testing requirements and approvals as full dredging episodes.

rows.verbatim:
That sediment provided for beneficial reuse shall be
sediment that would have otherwise been disposed of in-Bay or at SF-DODS.
rows.normalized: Sediment provided for beneficial reuse shall be sediment that would otherwise have been disposed of in-Bay or at SF-DODS.

rows.verbatim:
The volume of sediment for this method of mitigation shall be calculated based on the following
equation:
rows.normalized: The volume of sediment for this mitigation method shall be calculated using the specified equation.

rows.verbatim: The acres derived from the CDFW equation above shall then be multiplied by: (19,000 cy/acre).
rows.normalized: The acres derived from the CDFW equation shall then be multiplied by 19,000 cy/acre.

rows.verbatim:
any dredger under the LTMS
program that proposes to utilize hydraulic dredge methods would be required to comply with this
measure through conditions to their permit.
rows.normalized: If a dredger under the LTMS program proposes to utilize hydraulic dredge methods, it would be required to comply with this mitigation measure through permit conditions.

rows.verbatim: Adverse effects to longfin smelt DPS shall be minimized to the full extent possible.
rows.normalized: Project activities must minimize adverse effects to longfin smelt DPS to the full extent possible.

rows.verbatim: The Corps, EPA, and/or applicant shall minimize the potential for harm or mortality of longfin smelt DPS resulting from project related activities by implementing the proposed project as described in the 1999 Programmatic Biological Opinion, 2004 Amended Programmatic Biological Opinion, BA, and summarized in the Description of the Proposed Action in this biological opinion.
rows.normalized: The Corps, EPA, and/or applicant (including contractor) must minimize potential harm or mortality to longfin smelt DPS by implementing the project as described in the referenced Biological Opinions and BA.

rows.verbatim: The Corps, EPA and/or applicant shall ensure that their contractors or operators comply with this biological opinion.
rows.normalized: The Corps, EPA, and/or applicant must ensure their contractors or operators comply with this biological opinion.

rows.verbatim: The Service must be notified within 24 hours of the finding of any injured or dead listed species or any unanticipated damage to its habitat associated with the proposed project.
rows.normalized: The Service must be notified within 24 hours of finding any injured or dead listed species or unanticipated habitat damage related to the project.

rows.verbatim: When an injured or dead individual of the listed species is found, the Corps and EPA shall follow the steps outlined in the Salvage and Disposition of Individuals Taken section below.
rows.normalized: When an injured or dead listed species individual is found, the Corps and EPA must follow the Salvage and Disposition of Individuals Taken procedures.

rows.verbatim: Sightings of any listed or sensitive animal species shall be reported to the Service and the CNDDB (https://www.wildlife.ca.gov/Data/CNDDB/Submitting-Data).
rows.normalized: Sightings of any listed or sensitive animal species must be reported to the Service and the CNDDB.

rows.verbatim:
If evidence of a herring spawning event is observed within 500 meters of the
dredge immediately notify the following individuals:
rows.normalized: The dredge observer/contractor must immediately notify the listed individuals if herring spawning is observed within 500 meters of the dredge.

rows.verbatim: please ensure that the tracking data are being actively posted to the web, and that a project completion report is sent to EPA within 60 days of the completion of the work.
rows.normalized: The project (USACE/contractor) must ensure tracking data are posted to the web and send a project completion report to EPA within 60 days of work completion.

rows.verbatim: “Surface Disposal Zone” or “SDZ” is the 600 m radius circle at the center of the overall disposal site (latitude 37°39’N and longitude 123°29’W; NAD 83), within which the disposal vessel must discharge all of the dredged material.
rows.normalized: The disposal vessel must discharge all dredged material within the 600 m radius Surface Disposal Zone (SDZ).

rows.verbatim: Dredged material shall not be leaked or spilled from disposal vessels during transit to the SF-DODS.
rows.normalized: Contractor's disposal vessels shall not leak or spill dredged material during transit to SF-DODS.

rows.verbatim: Transportation of dredged material to the SF-DODS shall only be allowed when weather and sea state conditions will not interfere with safe transportation and will not create risk of spillage, leak or other loss of dredged material during transit.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall only transport dredged material to SF-DODS when weather/sea conditions will not interfere with safe transport or risk spillage/loss.

rows.verbatim: Disposal vessels must not be loaded beyond a level at which dredged material would be expected to be spilled in transit under anticipated sea state conditions
rows.normalized: Contractor's disposal vessels must not be loaded beyond a level expected to cause spillage in transit under anticipated sea states.

rows.verbatim: No disposal vessel trips shall be initiated when the National Weather Service has issued a gale warning for local waters during the time period necessary to complete dumping operations, or when wave heights are 16 feet or greater.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall not initiate disposal vessel trips during an active NWS gale warning covering the dumping period, or when wave heights are 16 feet or greater.

rows.verbatim: Uncharacterized dredged material, vessels, trash, and other debris are prohibited from being discharged at the site.
rows.normalized: Contractor is prohibited from discharging uncharacterized dredged material, vessels, trash, or other debris at the site.

rows.verbatim:
In order to exclude large trash and debris (including rocks) from
being disposed at the site, before transport to SF-DODS all dredged material must be placed
into scows through a steel mesh or chain “grizzly” with openings of no more than 12 inches
by 12 inches.
rows.normalized: Contractor must pass all dredged material through a grizzly with openings no larger than 12x12 inches before transport to SF-DODS.

rows.verbatim: Material retained on the grizzly must be removed and disposed of separately.
rows.normalized: Contractor must remove and separately dispose of material retained on the grizzly.

rows.verbatim:
Before any disposal vessel departs for the SF-DODS, an independent quality control inspector (“independent” means not
a direct employee of the permittee or dredging contractor) must certify in writing that the
vessel is not over-loaded, and otherwise meets the conditions and requirements listed on an
EPA-approved Scow Certification Checklist that contains all of the substantive elements
found in the example contained in the most current SMMP Implementation Manual.
rows.normalized: Before any disposal vessel departs for SF-DODS, an independent inspector must certify in writing that the vessel is not overloaded and meets the EPA-approved Scow Certification Checklist requirements.

rows.verbatim:
EPA and USACE must approve the proposed Scow Certification Checklist prior to the commencement
of ocean disposal operations.
rows.normalized: Ocean disposal operations cannot commence until EPA and USACE approve the proposed Scow Certification Checklist.

rows.verbatim:
No ocean disposal trip may be initiated until both the towing
vessel captain and the independent inspector have signed all relevant entries on the Scow
Certification Checklist.
rows.normalized: Contractor must not initiate an ocean disposal trip until both the towing vessel captain and the independent inspector have signed all required Scow Certification Checklist entries.

rows.verbatim:
The inspector shall provide a summary of any discrepancies or
inaccuracies on the Checklist in the permittee’s report to EPA and USACE for the relevant
month (see condition 10, below).
rows.normalized: The independent inspector shall provide a summary of Checklist discrepancies/inaccuracies in the permittee's monthly report to EPA and USACE.

rows.verbatim:
Disposal vessels in transit to and from the SF-DODS must
remain at least three nautical miles from the Farallon Islands whenever possible.
rows.normalized: Contractor's disposal vessels must remain at least three nautical miles from the Farallon Islands whenever possible during transit.

rows.verbatim:
Closer
approaches should occur only where the designated vessel traffic lane encroaches within 3
miles of the islands.
rows.normalized: Contractor's vessels should only approach closer than 3 miles to the Farallon Islands where the designated traffic lane requires it.

rows.verbatim:
The primary tracking system for recording
ocean disposal operations shall be disposal vessel- (e.g., scow- or hopper dredge-) based.
rows.normalized: The contractor's primary tracking system for ocean disposal operations must be disposal-vessel-based.

rows.verbatim:
Each disposal vessel shall have a primary navigation/tracking system functioning for each
disposal trip, calibrated for accuracy at a minimum at the beginning of each ocean disposal
project, that automatically and continually indicates and records the following information
throughout transportation to, disposal at, and return from SF-DODS:
rows.normalized: Each disposal vessel must have a primary navigation/tracking system operating each trip, calibrated for accuracy at least at the start of each project, recording specified data throughout transit to/from SF-DODS.

rows.verbatim:
This system must record these data at a maximum 1-minute interval while outside the SF-
DODS disposal site boundary, and at a maximum 15-second interval while inside the SF-
DODS disposal site boundary and the SDZ.
rows.normalized: The tracking system must record data at a maximum 1-minute interval outside the SF-DODS boundary and a maximum 15-second interval inside the boundary/SDZ.

rows.verbatim:
The primary system must also include a real-time display, located in the wheelhouse or otherwise visible to the helmsman, showing the position
of the disposal vessel relative to the boundaries of SF-DODS and its SDZ, superimposed on
the appropriate NOS chart so that the operator can confirm proper position of the disposal
vessel within the SDZ before discharging the dredged material.
rows.normalized: The primary tracking system must include a real-time display in the wheelhouse showing vessel position relative to SF-DODS/SDZ boundaries on an NOS chart before discharge.

rows.verbatim:
Within 24 hours of the completion
of each disposal trip, data recorded from the primary disposal tracking system must be posted
by a third-party contractor to a World Wide Web (Internet) site accessible by EPA Region 9,
the San Francisco District USACE, and NOAA’s Gulf of the Farallones National Marine
Sanctuary.
rows.normalized: Within 24 hours of each disposal trip's completion, tracking data must be posted by a third-party contractor to a web site accessible to EPA, USACE, and NOAA.

rows.verbatim:
The Web site must be searchable by disposal trip number and date, and at a
minimum for each disposal trip it must provide a visual display of: the disposal vessel transit
route to SF-DODS; the beginning and ending locations of the disposal event; and the disposal
vessel draft and load level in the bin throughout the transit.
rows.normalized: The posting web site must be searchable by trip number/date and must, at minimum, visually display transit route, disposal event locations, and draft/load level per trip.

rows.verbatim:
The third-party system must also generate and distribute “e-mail alerts”
regarding any degree of apparent dumping outside the Surface Disposal Zone of SF-DODS
(“mis-dumping”), and regarding any apparent substantial leakage/spillage or other loss of
material en route to SF-DODS.
rows.normalized: The third-party system must generate and distribute e-mail alerts for apparent mis-dumping or substantial leakage/spillage en route to SF-DODS.

rows.verbatim:
E-mail alerts for any disposal trip must be sent within 24 hours of the end of that trip to EPA Region 9, the San Francisco District
USACE, the relevant National Marine Sanctuary if the event triggering the alert occurred in
whole or in part within a Sanctuary boundary, and to other addressees as may be indicated by
EPA or USACE on a project-specific basis.
rows.normalized: E-mail alerts for any disposal trip must be sent within 24 hours of trip completion to EPA, USACE, and relevant sanctuary/addressees as applicable.

rows.verbatim:
A functioning back-up navigation system, meeting the
minimum accuracy requirement listed above, must also be in place on the towing vessel (tug,
if any).
rows.normalized: A functioning back-up navigation system meeting the minimum accuracy requirement must be in place on the towing vessel (if any).

rows.verbatim: at a minimum for each disposal trip it must provide a visual display of: the disposal vessel transit route to SF-DODS; the beginning and ending locations of the disposal event; and the disposal vessel draft and load level in the bin throughout the transit.
rows.normalized: The web site must, at a minimum, provide a visual display of the vessel transit route, disposal event start/end locations, and draft/load level for each disposal trip.

rows.verbatim:
In such cases the towing vessel’s position, and the tow cable
length and compass heading to the disposal vessel at the time of discharge, must be recorded
and reported.
rows.normalized: In back-up navigation cases, the towing vessel's position, tow cable length, and compass heading at discharge must be recorded and reported.

rows.verbatim:
Further disposal operations using a disposal vessel whose navigation tracking system fails
must cease until the primary disposal tracking system’s capabilities are restored.
rows.normalized: Disposal operations using a vessel with a failed navigation tracking system must cease until primary tracking capability is restored.

rows.verbatim:
In addition to the requirement in Special Condition 7 above for posting data on the Web, the permittee shall maintain daily records for each
disposal trip to include: the Scow Certification Checklist; the amount of material dredged and
loaded into barges for disposal; the location (reach, stations, or dredging unit/sampling area)
from which the material in each barge was dredged; the weather report for and sea-state
conditions anticipated during the transit period; the time that each disposal vessel departs for,
arrives at and returns from the SF-DODS; the exact location and time of each disposal; and
the volume of material disposed at the SF-DODS during each disposal trip.
rows.normalized: The permittee shall maintain specified daily records for each disposal trip, including checklist, dredged material amounts, dredging location, weather, transit times, disposal location/time, and volume.

rows.verbatim:
The permittee
shall also maintain, for each ocean disposal trip, both electronic data and printouts from the
GPS-based primary disposal tracking system (or the backup navigation tracking system when
appropriate) showing transit routes, disposal vessel draft readings, disposal coordinates, and
the time and position of the disposal vessel when dumping was commenced and completed.
rows.normalized: The permittee shall maintain electronic data and printouts from the GPS tracking system (or backup) for each disposal trip showing transit routes, draft, coordinates, and dumping times/positions.

rows.verbatim:
These daily records
shall be compiled at a minimum for each month during which ocean disposal operations occur,
and provided in reports, certified accurate by the permittee, to both EPA and USACE by the
15th day of the following month.
rows.normalized: The permittee shall compile daily records monthly (at minimum) and submit certified reports to EPA and USACE by the 15th day of the following month.

rows.verbatim:
For each ocean disposal trip, these reports shall include the electronic tracking and disposal vessel draft data on electronic media
approved by EPA and USACE, as well as hard copy reproductions of the Scow Certification
Checklists and printouts listed above.
rows.normalized: For each disposal trip, the required reports shall include electronic tracking/draft data on approved media and hard copy checklist/printout reproductions.

rows.verbatim:
The monthly reports shall include a cover letter describing any problems complying with the Ocean Disposal Special Conditions, the cause(s)
of the problems, any steps taken to rectify the problems, and whether the problems occurred
on subsequent disposal trips.
rows.normalized: Monthly reports shall include a cover letter describing compliance problems, causes, corrective steps, and recurrence status.

rows.verbatim:
The permittee shall
report any anticipated, potential, or actual variances from compliance with these Ocean
Disposal Special Conditions, and any additional project-specific Special Conditions, to the
District Engineer and the Regional Administrator within 24 hours of discovering such a
situation.
rows.normalized: The permittee shall report any compliance variances to the District Engineer and Regional Administrator within 24 hours of discovery.

rows.verbatim:
If any of these compliance problems occur within the boundaries of a National
Marine Sanctuary, the permittee must also report any such situation to the relevant Sanctuary
office within 24 hours.
rows.normalized: If a compliance problem occurs within a National Marine Sanctuary, the permittee must also report it to the relevant Sanctuary office within 24 hours.

rows.verbatim:
In addition, the permittee shall prepare and submit a detailed report of any such
compliance problems on a weekly basis by noon Monday, to the District Engineer and the
Regional Administrator.
rows.normalized: The permittee shall prepare and submit a detailed weekly compliance-problem report by noon Monday to the District Engineer and Regional Administrator.

rows.verbatim:
These reports shall describe the cause(s) of the problems, any steps
taken to rectify the problems, and whether the problems occurred on subsequent disposal trips.
rows.normalized: The weekly compliance reports shall describe problem causes, corrective steps, and recurrence status.

rows.verbatim:
Within 60 days
following the completion of ocean disposal operations, the permittee shall submit to the
District Engineer and Regional Administrator a completion letter summarizing the total
number of disposal trips and the overall volume (bin as well as in-situ) of material disposed at
SF-DODS for the project, and whether any of this dredged material was excavated from
outside the areas authorized for ocean disposal or was dredged deeper than authorized by the
permit.
rows.normalized: Within 60 days of completing ocean disposal operations, the permittee shall submit a completion letter to the District Engineer and Regional Administrator summarizing trips, volume, and any excavation/depth deviations.

rows.verbatim:
Except in accordance with the July 9, 2015 programmatic
Biological Opinion and July 20, 2015 revised Incidental Take Statement (ITS) issued by the
National Marine Fisheries Service for projects conducted under the LTMS Program [including
ITS section 2.8.4(a)(iii)] all ocean disposal operations, including transport to and discharge at
SF-DODS, must cease by midnight of November 30, 2026.
rows.normalized: All ocean disposal operations (transport and discharge at SF-DODS) must cease by midnight, November 30, 2026, except as covered by the referenced Biological Opinion/ITS.

rows.verbatim:
Otherwise, no ocean disposal operations are authorized beginning
December 1, 2026.
rows.normalized: No ocean disposal operations are authorized beginning December 1, 2026 (absent the referenced exception).

rows.verbatim:
The permittee shall provide a copy of the Dredging
Operation Plan (DOP) to the EPA at least 48-hrs in advance of the dredging episode that will
involve ocean disposal; this may be conveyed via email.
rows.normalized: The permittee shall provide a copy of the Dredging Operation Plan to EPA at least 48 hours before any dredging episode involving ocean disposal.
